at one point i went to a primary care doctor several times complaining of breast pain after i had my child, after examining me,she diagnosed me with a "cold" and sent me home with robitussin for my cough, when  instead i had mastitis which is an infection that i needed antibiotics for. which i later got after i visited the emergency room. 

that same doctor also made an inappropriate comment  while examining me by saying "oh you have big breasts your baby is getting a lot of milk" how ignorant and dumb  can a doctor be to not know that big breasts don't  mean a lot of milk production, that doctor was named dr zaw thanda. please refrain from seeing her if you do happen to be at the kaiser at panorama city. 

also kaiser says that they treat each patient as an individual, however that is not the case. they gave me a due date of october 14 however i kept telling them that a outside kaiser specialist   had given me a due date of october 22, they did not do any testing or even entertain that option to see why someone else would have given me that due date, when i didn't deliver by the 14th, they pressured to schedule to induce me saying that i was late to my delivery date, however i declined to get induced! and low and behold my baby was born on october 22, had i agreed to get induced i would not have had my baby naturally. 

also please refrain from seeing dr russell clayton in the obgyn department as well, horrible, horrible bedside manners, extremely rude and forceful with his thoughts and ideas, put me down for asking questions or disagreeing with him. there are several reviews on him as well on health grades i am surprised that kaiser permanente panorama city has not looked into this matter. 

these are just a few of my experiences at kaiser permanente panorama city, there are many more experiences, one even including  the lab were  they took several vials of blood from me when it wasn't even blood work that was needed or requested by any doctor. 

my wish is that kaiser permanente panorama city looks over the doctors knowledge thoroughly before hiring them and also looks at online reviews of doctors on health grades and other legitimate health websites and address any matters that patients have written reviews on.  

once again if you are with kaiser and choosing kaiser permanente panorama city as your main hospital please do your research thoroughly before moving forward. the only thing that i am thankful for is that they delivered my baby safely.

lets rate the emergency room today.
i went to the emergency room for a searing 9/10 hip pain, in tears and hysterical. i wasn't really aware of my surroundings but i did have my family with me. the only thing that helped was pacing, then laying in fetal and pacing again. they put me in a room, i paced out front of it crying quietly. then a nurse at the desk told me they preferred me stay in my room. i pleaded to her hysterically that it was the only thing that helped. she rolled her eyes at me so i kept on pacing. i was in front of my room, it's not like i was freaking out walking the hospital- i don't even believe i was sobbing loudly. 
when the x-ray team arrived they were so ginger and careful and understood me. however, they found nothing. not a darn thing. so i'm here. no answers, being told i'm fine, as i experience what feels like some on twisting a pitchfork in my hip and pulling my quad muscle from my femur and knee. pleasant yes? 
at this point my husband left me with my teen son to go get our other children from school.
a woman whom ,i'm assuming was a doctor, later appeared. and at this point i was in the phase of fetal rocking. she asked me to feel around on this lump on my hip. does this hurt? no. she pushed with moderate force on my hip, triggering a dull ache, i started to cry. she proceeds to tell me i have a lipoma, a fatty tumor, that doesn't really cause pain. then she disappeared after telling me they'll get a referral started and get me discharged. that's really all i could comprehend.
i started to pace again trying to relieve the agonizing pain from the area. i think i placed myself in the floor  sobbing. now thinking back was probably the grossest thing i could have done. a lady appeared, not a doctor. she began to tell me something about orthopedic and scheduling. i told her i didn't understand what she was asking. she asked me if i could schedule a visit. i told her i didn't know. she proceeded to say dates and times and i simply could not hear her over the pain. my son handed me my phone while i lay on the floor and i opened it. i clicked on some apps, i forgot what i was looking for. i asked again what i was doing. she told me dates. i couldn't for the life of me figure out what i was supposed to do so i started to cry again. she said something and left. i now realize that she was trying to schedule me an orthopedic and follow up appointment.
i started to pace, the fetal phase was no longer working, back to the hysteria walking phase. it had been 2 hours of hell. pure hell. someone showed up, a nurse i believe. she handed me some papers and told me to stick to my appointments and to go through the doors to the right. my son grabbed my items and i lead me down the hall. suddenly we were outside. i suddenly realized- they discharged me. i kept to my pacing and fetal on the bench. since my husband left to get my other children, my son and i stayed outside with no way home. turned away by the hospital, no relief from my living hell and no way home. 
this is lake norman emergency.

world-class care at a small regional hospital? who would have guessed, but it's 100% true. 

i'm an internal medicine physician (m.d; board-certified)
visiting from los angeles and was finishing dinner at a restaurant in boca with my 85 year-old dad on a saturday evening when he suddenly collapsed to the left and was having a stroke in front of my eyes. 

rushed him to boca regional medical center where they were already on high alert (we called ahead) and they implemented their "stroke alert" protocol with all hands on deck. 

on arrival, the (terrific) nurses whisked him directly from the front door to the head doc in the er (david leeman, md), he did a quick but thorough neurological assessment while dad was still in a hospital-provided wheelchair and sent him immediately to the ct scanner for a sophisticated brain perfusion scan. mind you, this all took no more than 6 minutes from er door to ct scanner (!).

ct scan showed no major blockages (thank g_d), but did show a small area that had subtly narrowed blood vessels and wasn't getting enough blood/oxygen to dad's brain for a short time. thus, the stroke symptoms at the restaurant. 

here's the best/mind-blowing part: within minutes, they had dad back from his ct scan and into one of the er's "critical care" beds, wheeled a two-way video monitor to dad's bedside and a top cleveland clinic neurologist-stroke specialist appeared live on screen and she did a remote bedside teleconsult (freshly-done ct brain perfusion scan on her computer) and chatted with/"examined" dad on the spot. 

she determined that dad had a "tia" (mini-stroke") but did not need (effective but sometimes dangerous) clot-busting drug treatment. after a team of (incredibly kind/efficient/competent) nurses took a detailed medical history, drew blood and did an ekg, they wheeled dad directly to the new marcus neuroscience inpatient unit of the hospital, where another team of great nurses attended to dad, gave him his evening meds and got him properly tucked in for the night. 

bottom line: from initial stroke symptoms to er admission to completed ct scan and expert consult/diagnosis to monitored inpatient bed, the whole process took less than 90 minutes. as stated above, world class care! 

grateful and impressed beyond words. if you need emergency care in boca, there's no better place to go

after 5 hours in the hallway, the er admitting physician dr. bernstein came around. he asked why we were in the er today. omg. so, i told him mom has heart failure and he said, "ok, we'll admit her."  i never saw him again.

about 2 hours later we were in a room. i asked who her doctor would be. no one was sure. two residents were roaming around.  i grabbed them and took them into a quiet room on the floor to explain mom's condition.  of course, they told me i wasn't a doctor so i should let them figure out what was wrong with mom. (i have been her only caregiver for 20 years. i know every med, all of her numbers, and am very aware of her heart condition.)  they said the best they could do was brief "a doctor" in the morning.  when i asked if he/she would be a cardiologist, they said, "no."

we waited until 7a the next morning. dr. foster spent 5 minutes with mom. he is an internist, not a cardiologist. the rest of the day we waited for an echo cardiogram or some diagnostics to be done to asses her condition. it never happened.

the nurses couldn't do much, since there is no doctor on the floor (no doctor on the floor) and nurses advised that internists are only available by phone and only in case of an emergency.

i asked mom's nurse dinesha to contact the two young residents who i had learned were on duty in admitting.  she called them at least 3 times over a period of 4 hours.  finally they arrived. they asked me the same questions over and over and over again. i was losing hope and patience.  i told them i wanted a cardiac consult now.

i am filing a complaint with medicare, the florida office of the inspector general, and contacting my congressman ted deutch.

i learned a big lesson and so i am sharing my experience so others aren't as naive as i was.  i was referred to the physical therapy group within presbyterian hospital dallas by my internist after having repeat back issues. i had to check in with hospital services, which should have been  a red flag since hospital charges are often much more than a private practice. i had a 1 hour evaluation where i was told i needed to work on my core muscles. i was encouraged to sign up for 1-2 sessions per week. i signed up for two per week, so i had one 1-hour evaluation and five 45 minute sessions.

i really liked the physical therapist. she was wonderful to work with. but if i had known the bill would be $3237 for these six sessions, i would have gone elsewhere. the bill was submitted to insurance, which was then  adjusted to their agreed upon price. i have to pay 100% out of pocket until i reach my deductible, so my 100% was $1578. that's $263 per session. i realize that the evaluation should cost more, but the five individual sessions included 5-10 minutes on an exercise bike -- something i could have done at home prior to arrival. this is such an insane amount for what was delivered in return and i'm no better than i was when i first walked into the place. i could have purchased at least a year's worth of exercise classes that focused on building my core instead.  

i sent an email to texas health voicing my frustration with not being told up front what my cost would be, but i haven't heard a word back, so i'm going to share my experience and hope others learn from my mistake. i'm guessing they don't care because i have to pay regardless and they're not going to do anything about it.  so... be forewarned... unless you have excellent health insurance coverage or medicare that will cover a certain number of visits, this is not the place to go for physical therapy. there are private practice physical therapists who charge much less so you can get more sessions for your money.

i am paying it down over 12 months, but it's the equivalent of having a car payment again and i really didn't need this expense right now. in addition to still having back issues i came here to address, i now have a huge amount of stress trying to figure out how i can come up with these monthly payments. lesson learned.

i'm giving 2 stars only because i liked my physical therapist.

having had previous, unavoidable experiences with robert wood's emergency room, it was with a mixture of trepidation and dread that i found myself once more walking through the emergency room entrance. previously, my father had often been a patient there due to a long battle with cancer which necessitated several trips to this particular emergency room.  at that time i had never before experienced such a complete disregard for basic patient care in an emergency room setting.
so when my elderly mother was transported there after a very serious fall this past week i was shocked as to how little has changed. this was a monday afternoon however you would have thought it was new year's eve - the waiting room was a war zone. at least forty people were cramped inside - patients were sitting on the floor - vomit was on the floors, in the bathrooms and even in front of the entrance! several heavily armed policeman stood looking menacingly at every person checking in. my mother was already in the er so i was waiting in line to check in. not knowing what her status was i was understandably anxious to get back to see her. however, i had to wait in line with patients that were checking in. as hipaa does not appear to be something that this hospital is familiar with, i was privy to most of these patients entire medical history. this was unavoidable as the receptionist loudly repeated it back to the patient, in front of all of us standing there. i became even more outraged when it became evident that most of the patients there were using the emergency room for their primary care - issues included stomach aches, slight fevers, colds, headaches, etc. - which were non emergencies and could have been dealt with at a pcp appointment. 
upon finally getting my "clearance" to go back to the emergency room (i had to have my id scanned - was told that weapons and/or drugs are not allowed - i felt like saying that the brooks brothers topcoat i was wearing does not have inner pockets large enough to hold a glock and meth just to be snarky however with two police officers glaring at me i felt it more prudent to just hold my tongue and press on).
once back in the emergency room i was disappointed to see that although the interior had been updated their view on quality of care remained the same. when my father was there he and several other patients were lined up on guerneys in the hallway for hours - one visit my father was in the hallway for 7 hours!
i arrived to find the same scene - row after row of patients lined up on stretchers against the walls. i found my elderly mother next to the nurses station covered in blood from severe facial lacerations. and then the wait began ..... one hour no nurse/no doctor; two hours the same; three hours the same. i was given a wash basin so i could wash the blood off my mom's face and hands. 
as this hospital once again has no conception of hipaa i found out from the team of doctors and nurses hovering over the patient in front of us that he came in with what he thought was chest pains - however he said it could have been indigestion from the two double cheeseburgers he ate. the young woman behind use was going through chemotherapy and was severally ill - once again staff went through her medical history for all to hear. 
i am generally a very patient person. i cannot begin to understand the stress that the staff in these settings are put under. however after 4 hours without a nurse or doctor even having the courtesy to stop and just apologize for the delay my patience was at an end. i stopped the nearest nurse and demanded that my mother be seen.
well amazingly enough a neurology intern and two nurses appeared out of thin air. they said it was busy but they would follow up and try to get my mother out of the hallway and into one of the er bays.
after 2 more hours she was finally moved to a semi private bay.
my niece who is a nurse practitioner arrived and thankfully took charge. the remainder of my mom's stay went relatively smoothly due to my niece's non stop advocacy.
however my niece was appalled by the condition of the facility. the bathrooms were filled with feces and urine, she found hypodermic needles in the elevator, the puddles of vomit in front of the entrance to the er remained there all day. 
in closing, avoid this emergency room at all costs! my mother will now be going to princeton medical center - a new facility that is clean with top flight staff where patients are treated as human beings and not objects of inconvenience.
also as an aside, during our "stay" in the er we kept noticing police and detectives running up and down the hallways - evidently there had been a "drive by shooting" in which 3 people were shot. individuals associated with the event were attempting to gain access to the er which had security on hyper alert. not the type of environment that i would want to expose any of my family members to again.

so this marks the first time i've "updated" a yelp review. while scca would in theory top the list of places i'd most want to upgrade to a higher rating, its scheduling department's ongoing incompetence once again caused enough stress and inconvenience today to warrant this downgrade to just one star.

quite frankly, i'd give the scheduling department (at least the one i'm stuck dealing with) zero stars if given the option. in my 10+ years as a patient, i've communicated with almost as many schedulers -- and perhaps one or two of them have been good at their jobs.

the one working when i first started treatment was so bad that after i once vented about her on a support board, a local person pm'd me to ask if i was talking about s***; she knew exactly who i was referring to (even though i didn't name names), and said the lady was notorious for her poor communication skills.

well, at this point, i actually miss that ten-years-ago scheduler. at least she never flat-out lied to me -- unlike the one two years ago who said it was ok when i questioned why my routine ct scan wasn't scheduled (see previous review), only for me to find out several weeks later, on the day i received the results for my bone scan, that yes, i did also need the ct scan (which i then had to have at the last minute, and wait an extra day to get results for -- as if regular "scanxiety" isn't bad enough without being made worse by lazy schedulers who can't be bothered to follow up on valid patient concerns).

after that 2018 incident, you'd best believe that i let scca know how i felt about it. i was then given some empty promise by patient relations that it "wouldn't happen again", they'd "communicate better", blah blah. because i'm a forgiving person, i thanked them and decided to let it go. 

i still have to initiate setting up all my appointments, despite always being told that the schedulers will "contact me" (and i'm actually ok with scheduling things myself; i do so on a regular basis with my gp's office, which has a specific portal for this, but apparently scca isn't yet that advanced. but why bother claiming that the schedulers will "contact me"?). still, things were more or less fine, until december of 2019.

that's when i contacted my onc's current scheduler to set up my every-three-months lupron injection, which i knew was due in january. she responded within a reasonable time frame, and told me that the shot was scheduled for 1/4.

right away, i noticed that this seemed too early; it's been made very clear to me over the years that these shots should be given every 12 weeks (though there is about a week's worth of flexibility; it doesn't have to be 100% exact).

but my most recent injection occurred on october 21st; and it shouldn't take a rocket scientist to see that 10/21 to 1/4 = not 12 weeks. it should take about 30 seconds to actually make the effort to count (or check a calendar, for crying out loud) and see that officially it's only 10 weeks and 5 days.

i emailed the scheduler with my concern. i pointed out that it seemed too early. i gave her the specific date of 10/21 as my last injection, so she had that information handy.

two days later, she replied; she mentioned the week's flexibility and said (and i quote; see attached) "it is okay for you to receive on 1/4". 

i knew it still wasn't quite even 11 weeks; and i certainly hadn't forgotten the incident two years ago. however, i decided to give this person -- who, after all, is paid to be thorough and accurate, and not make mistakes -- the benefit of the doubt and not question her further. i mean, i shouldn't need to be in a position where i'm asking "are you suuuure?" each time a member of my so-called "care team" relays a message to me. especially not after i'd handed this person her own error on a silver platter by pointing out the early date, and given her ample time and opportunity to follow up on and fix the error if needed.

fast-forward to today, january 4th. 

i don't blame scca for running behind, and for waiting until 20 minutes after my scheduled appointment to send me back to a room. i do, however, question why they waited until after i'd been sent back and had my vitals taken, to inform me that they couldn't actually give me the injection today... 

because it was too early. 

livid doesn't begin to cover how i felt after hearing this.

while lazy and irresponsible of them, i'll forgive scca for not bothering to call, or at least tell me when i checked in, that i wouldn't get the shot today; at least the infusion nurse who gave me the news seemed genuinely regretful, and made a visible (and appreciated) effort to help.

there is no excuse, though, to be flat-out lied to and misinformed again by a scheduler who can't be bothered to do her job. 

it's infuriating. it's ridiculous. and scca's patients deserve better.

i'll close with a line from my first review -- in short: i'd suggest looking elsewhere for treatment.

rushed my mother to williamson medical at 1 am this morning hoping to get relief from the writhing pain she was experiencing related to bladder cancer. despite having only one other patient, the er team was cold, harsh, thoughtless and entirely lacking in empathy. they were also mistaken in key parts of their diagnosis and their treatment. 

based on my experience today, i would never send a relative or a friend to williamson medical under any circumstance imaginable. 

why do these "healthcare professionals" feel they are serving their patients if they allow interminable delays (we were left for 2 hours without getting pain medication of any kind - the very reason we went in the first place) and brutish bedside manners (being moved from bed to gurney like a sack of potatoes, my mother getting screamed at during insertion of a catheter, blaming the patient for difficulty finding a vein {it took 3 tries and 3 pokes} in which to insert an iv, etc.).  10-minutes into the nurse screaming catheter insertion i heard the head nurse, amy, finally ask my mother what her name was. think about that. 

i found medical trash strewn all over the room we were in. this is 3rd world treatment and 3rd world quality care. 

i have great reverence for those who commit their lives to the serving and healing of strangers. i revere and feel hfriends who are er doctors, social workers, cancer scientists. these people serve mankind and they have empathy somehow baked into their dna. the er team at williamson medical should seriously consider why they chose to serve the public. i wouldn't hire any of the nurses or the doctor we dealt with to deliver my mail - they'd find a way to screw it up. they might, however, be just right to pick up our trash curbside.

to be fair, i should note we had generally positive experiences from the er check-in staff. also had acceptable treatment and care after getting my mother checked into the main hospital. but by the time we were upstairs, we had lost faith in the entire place, so we were watching/prodding them closely to be sure they attended properly to our mom. no one should need to do that. 

later in the day i spoke to an emt who said he wouldn't allow his friends or family to get taken to williamson medical er, that they have an awful reputation as a dumping ground for patients who have no advocacy and no close family oversight. his quote was "tell them to take you farther north to vandy, st. thomas etc. ". he also said, "even if you arrive at williamson medical without an infection, you'll surely leave with one". yikes.  wish i'd known. that's why i've labored over this review. beware. 

and my heart goes out to anyone reading this who has a loved one suffering like my mother has. god bless.

as you can tell if you look at how often i write reviews, i am extremely selective in my assessments. to cause me to write a review means you either hit a home run, or you struck out. unfortunately it's the latter with the emergency room of this hospital. we live within walking distance, and have lived in the community for 20 years +. in that time, we've used the hospital or the er just once or twice.  in other words, we're healthy, use regular doctors to meet our basic health needs, and are not the type of people who run to the er for a paper cut. additionally, we have truly excellent insurance supplied by our employers. 

with that as background, we visited the er at 1 am this week. my husband had been flat on his back with the flu/cold since returning from texas about 10 days ago. he was running a fever, coughing frequently, hadn't been able to eat, and was having trouble breathing. when we checked in we explained his symptoms and told them several times he'd been in international airports since coronavirus was starting to be talked about. when the er doctor sat down, he asked my husband "what's going on?" my husband very reasonably responded to that question by saying "i think i have the flu." the doctor shot back "i'll make the diagnosis." that sums up our experience in the er. they were generally detached, rude, and acted like we were bothering them by being there. the one exception was the truly friendly guy with the portable machine he rolled around to get a bit more info from patients such as religious preference. but the nurses and the doctor were awful. they didn't follow up with us about my husband being in houston airport (where the coronavirus was found), and when he complained about being lightheaded they initially ignored him and then reluctantly offered a wheelchair. they also debated between themselves as to whether they should offer an inhaler. once concluded, one trotted off to find the doctor. the other disappeared without telling us anything. a third employee sat staring at his phone, tapping away, and never said a word to us or looked our way even though we were perhaps 3 feet from him. i was standing the entire time and none offered me a chair.

as a community member, i don't feel los robles provided even minimally acceptable service. i looked on their website for a place to lodge complaints but there isn't one. interesting. additionally, there are more "1" ratings of this hospital on this site than "5" ratings. i'm not surprised by that.  i'm sure there will be an insipid follow up comment from jasmin o. saying "thank you for your comment, sorry we didn't meet your expectations" or something noncommittal like that. the fact that the hospital offers the same canned response to every poor review indicates to me that there is a lack of true caring.

everyone has bad days at work, i get that. but in certain industries, that can be dangerous. you don't want ticked off air traffic controllers, lackadaisical nuclear energy plant operators, or medical staff who lack compassion and don't really want to help patients. i expected more out of the er. we won't return; we'll go to an urgent care spot if needed in the future. which is too bad since los robles loses a future chance to over bill our very generous insurance company.

bottom line, i don't recommend anyone willingly going to this hospital's er based on our experience this week.

doc_text:
a good hospital overall, but be careful!  

my wife gave birth here in 2012.  when we arrived at around 1am, my wife was experiencing significant labor pains.  the triage staff didn't believe that she was in labor and refused to admit her.  they asked if she wanted a shot of morphine and we told them we thought she needed to be admitted but if it would help.  they basically said that it wouldn't help if she was in labor.  i said that we weren't doctors and asked for their medical advice.  they suggested that they try the shot to see if it worked and kept pushing the decision back to us.  we had no idea what to do, my wife was screaming, and we wanted the medical professionals to make a recommendation and stand by it.  it felt like nobody was willing to take accountability for the recommendation, but they also weren't willing to admit her.  ultimately, we let them give her the shot.

in giving it to her, they must have hit a nerve or caused some other permanent damage because that spot is sensive to this day and causes my wife significant pain whenever it is touched.

the frustrating part is that they were wrong, the morphine did nothing for her labor pains because she was indeed in active labor.  by the time they finally admitted her at 7:30a she was very dialated, they had to immediately give her the epidural, and our daughter was born only 4.5 hours later.

the delivery experience was great (largely do to the ob we had been working with as well as the nurse assigned) and we ultimately came back to deliver our son 4 years later.  i have also been impressed with the er docs there.  

that said, the pain my wife experiences due to the labor triage staff's negligence seems as though it will be permanent.  for that reason alone, because they needlessly and permanently insured her, i can only give this hospital one star.

hawaii's statute of limitations has likely run on this.  we had no idea that the damage would be permanent and little understanding at the time of how to handle it.  at this point, i feel that my only recourse is to recommend that others use caution and speak to an attorney immediately if you or one of your loved ones is injured by this hospital.

truly, almost everyone provided the sharp experience and you could tell the employees who really enjoyed their job versus the employees that view their job as just a paycheck. perception is everything. i actually took down names of those i found were the epitome of the "sharp experience" and those who need a little sprinkle of the "sharp experience" back into their lives.

i will start with the good. check in process was good. the er staff were quick with triaging and with getting labs/xrays/ekgs done before you even go to the room to be seen by the dr. we waited a long time , more than a couple of hours to be seen-but it was ok because we had heard the code being called overhead so i knew someone needed all the help they could get. cambria was my moms er nurse. she was awesome and always kept my mom and i up to date. she was personable and i really appreciated it. another shout out needs to go out to luv who is another er rn that was helping with my mom's iv. i thank you for your hospitality. 

there are 2 individuals that rubbed me the wrong way in how they approached my mother-they are the ones to why this review is 4 stars versus 5. i really wanted to mark this review as 2 stars but i didn't want to downplay the services of the employees that were really awesome.  one was a healthcare partner by the name of april and the other is kandra or kendra from the pharmacy. everyone but these 2 employees were friendly, others came and introduced themselves to my mother and i. april came in, no introduction. she just stated matter of factly that she was there to do an ekg. no smile, nothing. not sure if she worked a long day, however, that's not an excuse to be the way she was. kandra or kendra (her badge was flipped and could not see her name)from pharmacy...she was just plain rude and condescending. she came to ask my mother what meds she was on...mind you my mom had a list and by the time kandra showed up-my mom had shown 3 other people including dr.shipley the list of the 4 meds she is on. kandra came off as being annoyed or irritated that my mom didn't know her meds by heart. my mom told kandra that she had given the list to dr. shipley and kandra retorted "the problem is the dr.'s don't always document it. so you don't know the names? the doses?" and just kept asking the same questions using the same tone while staring up at the ceiling. hmmm...ok. how is this our monkey? that's not our problem that they don't always document it. what a way to throw another staff member under the bus. she was short when talking to my mom and honestly my mom and i were happy to see this employee leave the room. for my mom to sit there and say "what's wrong with her?" speaks volumes. some people need empathy training and she is one of them. they need to put themselves in the patients' shoes. guaranteed if kandra/kendra had brought her mother into this er and was approached by a employee who acted just like her-she would be upset too. she acted like she hated her job. that was my perception. so cold in her responses, no smile, just not sympathetic and makes me question why she is in healthcare to begin with. she was rude and cold, plain and simple. maybe it was a long day? back to the good. my mom was admitted onto 6 south. theresa (her pm rn), luz (pm aide) and joe p.(am rn)-i have nothing but the greatest things to say about these employees. hardworking, personable, helpful, always smiling, always keeping us updated, you guys have no idea how much i appreciated you and i know my mom appreciated you all just as much. i could tell all 3 of these employees love their job and love helping their patients. please make sure these 3 individuals get the recognition that they so deserve. sharp is lucky to have them on their team and we were really fortunate to have them taking care of my mom.

she stayed one night. i finally convinced her to switch to sharp and tomorrow i'll be calling to find her a primary care physician with sharp rees stealy.

how can you truly rate a hospital? based off of skill of drs/surgeons/np/nurses/cnas? of quality of care? quality of food(which we all know who have been in a hospital for any extended time can be atrocious)? how about all of the above!

i was admitted on 11/7 for a major surgery. not simple by any means and i am glad and blessed that this was the hospital i went to. aortic valve replacement which entails open heart surgery is scary enough to hear, but the team here at sharp memorial along with my surgeon dr. adamson put my fears to rest. from the initial consultation with him and going over what was to occur i felt at ease along with my girlfriend. even making jokes with me to relax me and calm my nerves just showed the bedside manner was well above par.

the complex is large and if you have multiple appointments in different buildings as i did. just ask the nurse assisting you to request a shuttle and they will get you to were you need to go. instead of moving your car over and over and dealing with the parking.

depending on what you're in for will dictate what floor/building you will be placed in. post op recovery icu is 2nd floor of main building and god bless if that's what you're in for.

nursing staff along with the np(nurse practitioner, don't call them a dr even if they're right there) have some of the most gentle care i've experienced from any hospital. i've bee. to other sharps and i can wholeheartedly say this hospital takes the prize. from providing you with as much information as possible to assist you in your recovery to ensuring you help is merely a call away by providing you with their direct number(they're given a cell phone at work so they can be reached by you or the nurses station if needed urgently) these ladies and gentleman embody care. my hats off to floor 6 (cardiac recover) for all the outstanding service and care they provided me. i honestly don't think i would have been recovering as well as i am without their support and care.

food is still none the less hospital food but i was able to speak with the chef in charge and here their plans for the coming year. adopting a comprehensive plan to ensure that the food quality and nutritional value are in keeping with the care provided at the hospital. a one of a kind program that already has made staples in improving the quality of the food and nutritional value(small steps so far such as switching from iceberg lettuce to green leaf lettuce and such). my hats off to them for improving this overlooked aspect in hospitals. the ordering system is fantastic how they take your meal order ahead of time to not interfere with your recovery and to ensure that you designated meal with restrictions if any get to you on time. i lived how each .real came with a nutritional overview letting you k ow nutrients, calories, etc in your meal. loved that!

radiology/radiologist as i had to deal with frequently were friendly and helpful. whether they had to assist me in my room or take me down to get mris(be aware, its always the coldest part of the building because they do have to keep those machines cool or they can burnout so ask for bra blanket if you need it). the transport team who assisted you getting from location to location or helping you leave in the end were always kind, helpful and made sure you knew you were always welcomed back.... hopefully not soon though.

all in all if i could rate this hospital a 11 or higher i would! excellent is the only word i can come up with to describe the care provided by the staff at sharp memorial. my hats off to all the staff that help in the recovery of the many patients who walk through their doors and the supporting staff behind the scenes.

wow, i wish i had seen these other reviews before sending my mother here. her (our) experiences were a nightmare - with the list of grievances almost too long to list. she went to chcc following a bout with pneumonia. we selected chcc because i live in wyckoff, it was convenient and we thought it had a decent reputation. what a mistake. the aides and nurses don't work together and have a very "not my area" lack of responsibility. my mom was in the rehab center for over a week before she received her first shower. the bogus explanation was she was a two person assist and couldn't be put into the shower - really? she had been in a prior rehab center, we have seen the shower seats and the lifts used for immobile patients. the bottom line was understaffing of the aides and laziness on the part of staff.

there is also a lack of accountability and lack of oversight by administration. my mother was finally given a shower and had her hair washed after my insistence to speak to the head nurse and whomever ran the facility. even after complaining many of the same problems continued.  she wasn't washed again for another week after the first complaint.

my mom is immobile and incontinent. she too had issues with infrequent changing and dirty diapers. i had taken mom for a wheelchair ride one day and she told me she needed to go to the bathroom. we went back to the room, and i rang the call button. when the aide came in, she told me mom required two people to get her on the toilet so i should just let her dirty the diaper and then she would change it - is this someone's perverse definition of patient dignity? 
she's also been prone to urinary infections so we are careful to make sure she isn't sitting in a wet diaper. we were told, when we asked about frequency of changing, they have super absorbent diapers so we shouldn't worry.  how about just changing her more frequently? why was that not an option?

then there was the day my mother spilled water at lunch all over her floor - again we called the call button. first we were told maintenance was out of lunch and they would come later.  four hours and 5 or 6 calls later, the water was still there. it was not cleaned up until one nurse saw i was about to lose it - and she brought towels and cleaned it up herself. i regret i didn't take her name as she was the only person we encountered who acted like they cared.

the food can be ok but only if you carefully select from the menu - if you leave it up to regular choices, beware. we mistakenly ordered a tuna sandwich one day - it was disgusting. there were two pieces of white bread, a smear of tuna fish that was thinner than the amount of butter most people put on toast and that was it - no lettuce, no tomato, nothing nutritious about it. their idea of a good diet is interesting - again if you order a protein, a salad and some vegetables you have a chance at a decent meal, but beware if you aren't diligent about your loved ones food. my mother's roommate had to eat sandwiches because of an injury, she told her daughter one day she would rather not eat than to eat another one of those sandwiches.

bottom line - if my mother needs to go to rehab again, i can tell you where we won't go.

my dad just died here with homeless people walking around the first floor non-stop.

the nurses and surgeons were amazing.  he had a heart attack and he was rushed into surgery but he was on the damn eliquis which complicated things.  we got an amazing surgeon and he somehow came out of surgery... but had internal bleeding from eliquis and had to be rushed back in later the next morning.  then it went downhill from there.  

again, the nurses were all super nice and attentive.  two surgeons, about four doctors, and every nurse was great.  but... one doctor (a fellow), goupta, his bedside manner flat-out sucks.  my dad was dealing with a lot of things... but when we had to talk to him, he was waiting in the room, eating something, on his phone.  then when we walked in, he finished up his phone, put it away and was cold as ice, completely going through the motions, no expression, crumbs on his face from what he was eating before we walked in (in the waiting area).  he couldn't have given a damn less.  just another patient.  he was asking up about doing cpr but telling us to 'not' do cpr if my dad had an episode.  i asked, well, that's a major thing to say... so why not?  he didn't give any kind of explanation, basically he's just too sick to save.  so, we later asked someone else and they said there's an 80% chance of puncturing the heart with the wires from surgery.  okay, now that was crucial information that this robot didn't tell us.

another idiot, heartless doctor was walking a group of fellows from bed to bed and my mom was with my dad.  he callously walks by my dad, looks at the numbers, "not good, not good," (with her sitting there) and then walks to the next patient.  wtf?  if he's "not good," you whisper that outside of the earshot of wife sitting right there!  you word it like, "it's going to be challenging, etc."  these aren't cars getting oil changes... these are people.

also, the homeless people on that first floor is absolutely out of control.  willie is one guy they know by name but nobody does a damn thing about it.  security is short-staffed and nobody sits at the front door at the desk.  willie stinks so bad that you can literally smell where he walked.  he goes into the bathroom, unloads, then walks around, then out... then security sprays aerosol to hide the smell.  then various other people asking us, while waiting for my dad (when we were outside of the icu) for money, for coffee, etc.  there is one bathroom for everyone to use... one... and the homeless people go right for it every time.  one guy was taking a sink shower in one of the three sinks, with his disgusting, contaminated stuff all over the other sinks.  i had to ask him to move it.

first of all, this is supposed to be a sterile environment and this hospital does not take it seriously.  we asked security why someone wasn't at that entrance 24/7.  they said that there's no budget for it, the hospital won't pay for a body to sit there.  wow.  all of that money coming in here and they can't pay for security.  they can literally walk right right into the recovery area because those doors automatically open.  the most critical patients are sitting ducks if they walk past the vending machines and into the room.  it's going to take just one preventable incident and a huge lawsuit to wake this hospital up.

anyway...

my dad died.  i don't want to blame the care, they seemed great and attentive.  someone was always with him.  however, i also noticed that none of the other patients were recovering either.  not one.  i saw a couple who died, though.  it was pretty grim.  i kept saying, "i just want to see one of these families have some good news."  i realize it's a super critical area but man, i dunno.  

if i had a choice, honestly... i would keep the two surgeons... but recover in a different hospital, if we could.  it's literally life or death.

choose your hospital wisely:

i went to holy cross for a knee replacement.  the doctor was great and replacement doing good. however, when i came home i was on pain meds with tylenol.  doctors told me i most likely acquired a gram negative ecoli infection from the urinary catheter. the infection then grew into my blood and i became sepsis. after a week in another hospital and sent home with a mid line iv for antibiotics. i recovered after three weeks. i called holy cross hospital infectious department to let them know.  well i received no concern, no caring, and an excuse that i only had the catheter for one day. they also said, in order to pick up this infection in the hospital i would have had to have the catheter two days.  so not a very educated answer.  infections are acquired through direct contact and time exposure plays no role. 

copied from the internet:

causes
bacteria are normally found throughout the body including on the skin and in the intestines. when kept in balance, bacteria can help the body work normally. however, an imbalance of the bacteria or passing of bacteria to areas where there are no bacteria, can lead to an infection. an infection will develop if large amounts of bacteria are present, the bacteria are aggressive, or the immune system is weakened.

common ways for bacteria to pass to vulnerable parts of the body include:

use of medical devices that pass into the body, such as iv or urinary catheters
open wounds
contact with someone who has or has been exposed to gram-negative bacteria
risk factors
hospitalization is the most common risk factor for gram-negative bacterial infections. the longer the stay in the hospital, the higher the risk of infection.

other factors that increase the risk of a bacterial infection include:

recent surgery
use of urinary catheter
war wounds
dialysis for kidney disease , which includes regular use of iv lines or catheters
mechanical ventilator use
weakened immune system

with my experience it doesn't matter how good the doctor is.  if the hospital is a sick hospital, even the most mild surgery could cause sickness or even death. do your research.

mclaren's billing:

my husband had a stroke december 2019. he was rushed to mclaren northern michigan hospital in petoskey. frankly, i felt my head was in a fog most of the time and i was just so glad he came out of it alive. he had rehab done locally in january and had to have a follow-up with the neurologist february 3rd. doctor said that they cannot find a reason for my husband having a stroke and he needed to have a loop recorder placed inside his chest to see if he has a-fib.  february 7th he has that put in.  today (february 26) i am sitting at my desk paying $1,300 in co-pays for the things he had done - i admit it is a bit steep for us but praising god my husband is still alive. however, as i was paying by phone with mclaren, they let me know that there was a bill for $11,000.00 coming down the pike that wasn't covered by bcbs. it was the loop recorder. they called and asked for a pre-authorization for the loop to be placed in and was told by bcbs that they didn't one - no mention that it wasn't a covered benefit; the doctor's office didn't ask and bcbs didn't offer them the information. how does two retired people on social security suppose to pay for their mistake because each one blames the other for not getting the information and we are stuck with the bill? 

paying on these bills are equally as hard because all you get from mclaren's is the dollar amount - you really have no idea what you are paying on (it isn't itemized). also, when paying online through your bank, you have to input each bill into your system as each bill has its own unique account number. so you may have a dozen bills (like we have) and each one has its own account number - very time-consuming having to pay online.

the physical therapists were two older teens who helped me walk across the hall once and then showed me how to push a walmart bag back and forth while i sat in a chair.  i was never given a discharge meeting and was told ten minutes before i was picked up that an ambulance was coming to transfer me.  it was friday and they do not want to staff over the weekends so everyone was supposed to leave by noon.  i believe the kids might have been summer employees as it was summertime.

my experience with overlook started with labor & delivery. i was scheduled to be induced on a tuesday. i had been warned ahead of time that since i was an elective induction, i could be bumped if other medically necessary inductions or women in active labor came in that same day, which obviously i understood. however, the communication with labor & delivery that day was horrible. they kept asking me to call back every two hours to check in to see if they had a bed for me. when we would call them, it would take 10 minutes to get someone on the phone who could provide an update and then we find out in the afternoon that my doctor didn't even know i was on the schedule for an induction that day. i didn't get induced until the following day and i do have to say, once we were actually there, the nursing staff was great.

then i get moved to the mother baby unit, which was the most horrible experience. the first issue was that it was amazon rainforest hot in there the entire stay. we spoke with various staff members including engineering about lowering the temperature only to be told that the unit was already on their winter setting and nothing could be done about the temperature. however, for about 3 hours in the middle of the day, there was actually antarctic cold air that blew out of the heat/ac unit, which contradicted the fact that the unit was already on the winter setting. the cold air was a welcome temperature change given how hot it was in there the majority of the time, but even cheap motels have better climate control. 

the experience with the techs was horrible as well. the amount of times they came in to take my blood pressure, take blood, etc. was absurd and never coordinated with other tests being performed so someone was walking into my room to do something to me or my baby what seemed like 100 times a day at all hours of the day and night. while i know that this is somewhat just the way it is when you stay at a hospital, they typically weren't even nice about it, it was like we were just a job they had to do and move on to the next one.

here are two specific horrible tech experiences. 2 techs came in to help me get out of bed 12 hours after my surgery. obviously i struggled to get out of bed and they were essentially nasty to me about the fact that i was slow. i then asked if i had to get up to go to the bathroom again should i call for them or was i pretty much on my own to do it. seeing how unhelpful they were i figured this would be the case and sure enough, they told me i was on my own. 

another morning, it was about 4 am. myself, my baby, and my husband were all sleeping, which was pretty obvious considering the lights in our room were out. a tech walks in, turns all the lights on, and proceeds to stick me with a needle to take blood right as i woke up to see her doing so. again, if this was something that absolutely had to be done at that time, she could have at least been more considerate in warning us that she was going to be turning on the lights and taking blood instead of just storming in and waking us all up and not even telling me why you are there before sticking me. 

and i have to mention that since overlook is baby friendly, the baby is with you 24/7. so after having major surgery, you need to care for your baby, and then they come into your room 100 times a day so i probably slept for 5 minutes the entire stay. 

after having so many medical staff in and out of the room every day, the cafeteria staff also asked you to fill out the menus and then if you didn't get to it when they wanted it done, they were nasty to you about that. but then after meals were brought, the dirty trays would sit in the room for hours to the point where we would stick it outside the door just to get it out of the room. 

then the day of check out, they say to be ready to leave by noon, which we were more than happy to do since we couldn't wait to get out of there. but instead of having an actual discharge procedure and having our paperwork ready to go, we had to call the nurses station twice before the paperwork was brought to us and it was definitely after 12 and then the person at the nurse's station was nasty to my husband after we had to call a second time to see what the status of the paperwork was. all the while they make you pay for parking. my husband had to make a few runs home for some things and each time they made him pay. tens of thousands of dollars for a hospital stay and they nickel and dime you on the parking. oh but don't worry they validate you so you only pay 2$ instead of 7$. all in all my husband paid close to 16$ extra for parking in their overcrowded and dirty lot.

needless to say, this stay was miserable and i'd rather go through another actual c section surgery than have to stay another few days in the mother baby unit. the only reason i even gave two stars is because the majority of the nurses were good.

i am a registered nurse and was transferred to this hospital from our birthing center because i failed to go into natural labor on my own. i have been a nurse for ten years on an impatient level so i knew what types of interventions i may have to have and was assured my wishes would be respected. that is exactly opposite of what happened. this hospital on their website claims to support low intervention births and that is not the case. 
for example, i wanted to walk in the hallway. it took hours and a really persistent saint nurse jac to let me do so, and then their signal was so poor i only could walk a short distance. this is not a huge request, walking has shown to help labor progress and they should have equipment to be able to accommodate. 

our doula was not respected by the staff and management and wasn't allowed to do any of the things all the other area hospitals allow her to do as a birth professional. she has been allowed in the room for epidurals and c-sections at all the other area hospitals, this is not a new or unusual request. 
the charge nurse sarah insisted on throwing a paper in my face that i had signed about their policies and being extremely rude. part of their rules were on the back of a paper and i hadn't even seen that section because the place for me to sign was on the front.
we unfortunately had to argue to get them to allow our midwife in for a short visit. she was not doing any patient care, just wanted to be supportive. we did have a couple standout nurses (jac, alanna, stephanie) that did their best but it's obvious their hospital policies are not supportive of natural birth.

the manager told us that we should have gone to another hospital if that's the type of care and birth we wanted to receive. she also told our midwife our family was disruptive in the waiting room but never told my family or us that they were disruptive at all. she should have come out to the waiting room to handle the disruption (if it even existed) as a manager, but that was never done. due to their strict visitor policy before birth my father had to wait for 48 hours in that waiting room and wasn't able to see me even for five minutes, so maybe he was a little frustrated. it is obvious to me as a nurse that leadership will round to see if you have any problems but make it clear they have no desire to change or consider policy changes.

i was promised i would get to do skin to skin right after the birth, yet they wouldn't let me hold or see my perfectly healthy son until i was out of the operating room. our birth center no longer recommends this hospital unless it's an emergency. if you are wanting a low intervention birth go to another hospital. you have the right to be respected and you have choices in your birth. don't make the same mistake and let yourself be bullied like i was

the admissions office is full of miserable, negative people who appear to be angry all the time. i asked this one woman if i could show her our health insurance care and she goes: that's fine, honey. bring it back later. so an hour or so later, my mom gets her own bed in the er and tells me to go show them our insurance, before they send a huge bill to our house. i went back and the same lady who attended us began to scold me. she asked me why i did not register my mom with an admissions staff member inside. i told her that i was not aware that i had to do that. she goes, your mom will be charged $40k for services at the er today. i asked why? if we have insurance. it does not make sense. so i had to speak with one of their co workers who was nice enough to help me, but at the same time, had a disgusted face attitude as if she wanted to throw me into space.

now the er....  there were a few decent human beings working in there but there were two idiots working there that made me question: how the hell did you get a job here?
the first nurse who attended us, questioned why i was helping my mom walk into her room, if she has movement in her legs. i tell him, they took our wheelchair and she is a lot of pelvic pain, which is affecting her ability to walk normally. didn't bother to hold the door or help us and responded with an "oh".

the next nurse that helped me mom comes in: ma'am, when was the last you have seen a gynecologist? she responds 15 years ago, i had a hysterectomy done and i had both ovaries removed, due to fibroids in this hospital. she goes, you have an ovary and the ct shows that you have a 4cm mass on the ovary. we were really upset about what they found, but my biggest concern was that they did not bother to admit her, nor run a biopsy to determine if it was cancerous or not. she just said: take your mom to her pcp, they will help you out. i go, your not going to help her? she's in pain and you're not going to administer any morphine or pain killer? or prescribe pain meds? she says... no, it's not our specialty. ask your pcp to refer her to a gynecologist/oncologist. 

honestly, this hospital visit was horrible in so many ways, but it's like why do people get treated like a commodity in a hospital? i feel like patients are seen as an object of waste, rather than as a human being that needs all the attention and care that they deserve. what's more sickening is that private health insurances pay these hospitals to provide health services to patients, but many people will take advantage of that money and not help their patients.

my mom unfortunately has cancer but we know deep down that she will be healed by the lord. miracles do happen and no one deserves to receive medical negligence like my mom did from this dump. beware of medical negligence/medical malpractices. they account for 250,000 deaths each year. no one deserves to die this way. 

never will we ever set foot in this hospital.

i'm a labor and delivery traveling rn and have been to many hospitals over my 18 years of travel nursing.  i wanted to take the time to write a review of this hospital because i am very, very impressed with the care and service that they give their labor and delivery patients.  
the rooms are not as big or flashy as sutter or kaiser, true, but the nurses are kind, intelligent, and very caring.  they know their stuff, as the hospital is able to accept high risk patients from the area.  their c section rate is very below the national average (i heard it was 10% which is amazing) and they have a really wonderful lactation consultant that sees patients all week.  every patient gets a social work visit as well, in case they have personal issues they might need help with.  midwives attend most deliveries but the obs are very non interventive and will respect individual wishes.  eating in labor is normal as well as using mobile monitors or just being intermittently monitored to begin with. there are no prima donna surgeon types here and i so appreciate that.  the coffee they bring to the floor is starbuck's, and the food will improve when their kitchen renovation is complete!  all in all, it's one of my favorite hospitals i have ever worked in!

i was 35 weeks and 5 days pregnant when i visited this hospital.
i was at home when i felt intense pain in my lower uterus. i didn't know what it was but i knew for sure it 1.) was not labor because it was an isolated spot and not my entire uterus and 2.) wasn't normal because it felt like a chainsaw or a fire inside me, like i was being ripped apart from the inside.
this hospital is a half mile away from my house so it was convenient to come here. the nurses in l&d were extremely sweet and tried their best to console me even though i was screaming my head off. i was hooked up to monitors but not an ultrasound so all they saw was contractions but didn't see what was going on inside me. they assumed i was in early labor, when i actually wasn't (but they did not find that out until after my delivery 5 hours later, so i 100% don't blame them for thinking i was). they administered 3 shots of some safe drug to slow down labor but it didn't make a difference (again, because i wasn't in labor) so they admitted me to a delivery room. i was offered an epidural and didn't hesitate to scream yes.
the epidural changed everything and now i was a happy camper. the delivery doctor, dr. renan, came in to tell me gently "we might might have to do a c section, because the baby's heart rate is dropping with each contraction, but we might not, we will see what the ultrasound reveals." i was hoping that wasn't true at all, as a c section delivering a preemie was not at all in my vision. i waved it off and said ok whatever. the us revealed my placenta was almost 80% detached (this is called a placental abruption) so he kindly told me he would "try to speed up my labor to get this baby out naturally". he was about to leave the room when my water broke all on it's own on the bed. it was 10% water and 90% bright red blood. with a smile on his face (to calm me down) he said in a sweet, caring tone, "ok, your placenta is detached, we are doing an emergency c section, it will be ok!" i began bawling and saying i didn't want that but the nurses told me it needed to happen. (i later found out 3 hours postpartum that i was actually 5 minutes from death at that moment, but they didn't want to act frantic to scare me more, which i really appreciate!!) 
within minutes i was in the or and they were cutting me open. fortunately i felt nothing. i kept looking at my husband telling him i was scared i would feel pain and then suddenly i heard my daughter squeak and the other surgeon said "baby is out". i hadn't even felt it! crazy! after they gave her oxygen and saved her life, they brought her to my face so i could kiss her and tell her i loved her. we locked eyes. she was perfect. my husband then followed her to the nicu while i was stitched up. 
first of all - my incision is amazing!!! i'm 12 days pp as i type this and i'm completely out of pain, and the scar is like 5 or 6 inches and so thin it's not even noticeable. it's still a little bruised but as soon as those go away i'm 100% confident no one will ever know i had abdominal surgery this summer when i'm in a bikini. i couldn't be more grateful to dr. renan for acting quickly and professionally to save our lives, and at the same time make it a cosmetic procedure to ensure i'd still have a slamming body afterwards. then there was the nurse who stayed with me in the recovery room for 2 hours after the surgery. she talked to me like we were best friends and made sure i was emotionally stable until my husband came back. she didn't leave me for a second. i felt so safe with her. her name was lilley.

nicu:  the nurses are friendly, answer all questions, are extremely respectful to parent wishes, informative, & amazing with preemie babies. i love all of them. especially lily & christine
my daughter was there for 7 days. during her stay i only left for several hours at a time to sleep in my own hospital room. once i was discharged i spent the next 3 nights on the couch in her room so i could bf her. they just let you sleep in your baby's room there! it's amazing! 
like i said, they respect parent wishes - i said no bath for 2 days, they obliged. i said no pacifiers, they said ok. i said bf only, they never gave her formula.

every day i was there i was visited by a lactation consultant to help me feed her. every other day a social worker came in to talk to me about my feelings like a therapist. i had an extremely traumatic week having an unexpected delivery, a c section, and a nicu baby. i was traumatized by the situation - not by anyone who helped me and my daughter. in fact, the only reason i'm not currently cookoo insane right now is because of how everyone treated me. everyone was so gentle, so sweet, so informative and respectful.... i'm just over the moon appreciative for everything they all did for me. i can never pay them back.

doc_text: i brought my 16 year old son here today after 6 days of fever (flu diagnosis at urgent care and upper respiratory infection diagnosis at his doctors office just yesterday). unfortunately, he was a lot worse this morning and his doctor doesn't see patients on friday. we signed in and they immediately ordered a chest x-ray and blood work and had us go back to the waiting room. after being called back for the blood work, they sent us back to wait for the x-ray. about 10 minutes later, my son said everything was "going black" and he felt so sick, and he became gray in color, shaking, and clammy. i wanted to run for help but i couldn't leave him sitting there because he felt like he was passing out. i asked a woman sitting nearby to please ask the security guard to get help. he immediately went for help while another patient yelled for a doctor. the nurse came right out and brought him back to a room, he was shaking, so out of it, and so gray in color...he was going into shock, and needed to lie down. thankfully the charge nurse (i found our later her name is gerri) rushed in and had him in a gown and on the bed so quickly, all the while telling him what she was doing, telling him she knows he doesn't feel well, and reassuring both of us that she was going to start an iv and get him feeling better. she was amazing! kind, compassionate, and incredibly efficient. i honestly felt that he would be ok as soon as she took over. it was a bit of a blur after that, but gerri and his other nurse who took care of him for the majority of the time we were there (joyce) brought warm blankets, reassured him, was made us feel like our son was getting the care he needed. joyce  was very kind and caring also, and checked in with us often, even calling multiple times to find out the status of the chest x-ray. we found out later that this was their busiest day in years, and gerri and joyce both took the time to make sure our son felt safe and well cared for, and made me as a mom feel so much better. i can't thank these 2 nurses enough for taking such good care of my son. they both deserve 5 stars, the only reason i put 4 is because the first nurse didn't handle the situation well and showed no compassion, and very little competence. maybe she was having a bad day...maybe she's seem this too many times...but for my son and myself, this was a terrifying experience. i feel so grateful that gerri stepped in and took control of the situation, and handled it with such empathy, professionalism, and efficiency. thank you, gerri and joyce!

i was admitted to antelope valley hospital as a trauma patient early last month after a terrible head on collision. initially the trauma nurses were great until the ct scan. a woman who was in the ct scan room asked the man who was wheeling me in if he asked if i may be pregnant. "that's not my question to ask" is what he said. then she asked me directly if there was a chance that i could be pregnant and i said yes. after that the entire staff seemed extremely annoyed, and didn't end up even administering a pregnancy test before the ct scan. although this was very upsetting i wasn't in the state of mind to bring any more concern on the matter.

they then put me in the emergency room and eventually came in to tell me i had a fractured l5 vertebrae, and fractured fibula on my left leg. i knew something was wrong with my right foot but they insisted that nothing showed up in the ct scan. they ordered a cam boot for my left leg then tried to put it on the right instead. a common theme in my 5 days here was that i had to inform almost every staff member of my own injuries and i wasn't even confident that they had diagnosed everything properly.

i had two mris done because i kept complaining about my foot. it wasn't until the 4th day that they found 2 fractures in my right foot. this was extremely upsetting after a ct scan and x-rays on my feet, and the doctors kept promising that i would go home the next day after day 2.

i spent the first night and second day in the critical care unit, which most of the nurses there were extremely attentive, i believe angela was the name of the rn i had during the day and she was great. once they moved me out of critical care the second night, it all went extremely downhill.

the remaining 3 days consisted of an average wait of 30-45 minutes for any nurse to assist after i pushed the button (especially during the night time) and a lot of rough handling when transporting me anywhere. keep in mind i have a fractured spine vertebrae and (soon to realize) three total leg/foot fractures between my two legs so i could not do more than roll on to my side, let alone sit up/stand/walk. this is incredibly disappointing beings how i am only in my 20s and someone who would seriously need help could possibly not have their call answered in a timely manner.

the two other nurses that stood out to me were stephenie (rn) and sherri (nt). sherri, who was very nice and talkative, unfortunately spent entirely too long speaking with patients about her personal life. she was the one i had the biggest problem with answering my calls. after 45 minutes, i sent my husband to find her, then 30 minutes later she came back in a rush and told me i just needed to be patient. i'm sorry but waiting over an hour for a bed pan because i can't walk myself to the restroom is ridiculous. this seemed like a common theme before shift change that the wait times would get longer and longer.

stephenie on the other hand, was the best nurse i had. she answered my calls promptly (usually within 5 minutes),was very informative, gave me a lot of supplies and products to maintain my hygiene, and helped clean my tables often. she was very nice and offered a lot of emotional support as well as she was my nurse on day 4 and i was ready to get the f out of that place.

all in all, if you are not a trauma patient, please go elsewhere. that is the only reason i had to go here and although i am grateful for the staff members that truly helped, i wish that my experience was different.

after spending months in the sicu fighting cancer, my husband passed away several months ago at med city dallas. i've started this review so many times i can't count, but i was so mentally drained, i kept pausing it. i wish i could say my beautiful husband got the best care. instead, we were hit by the harsh reality of complete disrespect and disregard for human suffering. patients don't normally stay in the sicu for long time, so the nurses can wear smiles for few days. we were there for months and got to see their real faces.

it started with me finding countless bruises, head bumps, blue skin indentations, scratches, bloody marks, skin tears, tube lids and saline syringes under my husband embedded in his skin. i kept finding him with wounded neck bent in such a way he was grimacing in pain, no one bothered to check and help. i was finding him lying with dirty face/ears/eyes, lips chapped covered with white pasty layer, chest covered with sticky residue from the electrodes, no one cared to wash it off, room dirty, feeding bags hanging over 24 hours, floor dusty, stained with dry formula, the list goes on. i kept complaining and they hated me for it. 

i took a lot of photos and involved patients advocate crystal crawford. those photos shocked everyone we know, yet crystal kept saying "when i'm there, they are so nice with him..."...like i was lying. it was useless. so i contacted the sicu director mark sanders. to justify their mess the nurses decided to gang up and roll it all on me. yes, i did raise my voice when confronted them, i was mentally and physically exhausted spending 8-10 hours with my husband, i was grieving. what was their excuse for yelling, calling me names, slamming doors, drawers, kicking me out of the room and badmouthing me? mark sanders was no help either, even called to tell me that nurses feelings were hurt and that "their tears were real". and my tears? they need to suck it up, it's icu, people are suffering. it was my loved one who was dying, not theirs! mark sanders offered to move us to a different unit, but after that he just vanished. i then contacted chief nursing officer joy sully. i left her voicemails, messages with her assistant, even a handwritten letter for her at the front desk pleading to move us to different icu, away from poisonous atmosphere, to give us peace. but she too ignored it. they didn't want to bother with the dying man. 

our last weeks in the sicu was a nightmare. every day was a different nurse, "fragile" them couldn't handle demanding wife for 3 shifts in the row. i made them face every neglect and they couldn't stand me for it. once they sent a nurse w. from the night shift. that nurse did a number on my husband. she left him lying in feces for hours, didn't check as often as she was supposed to and that created more skin erosion, she was so reckless that his peg tube popped out of his stomach, and finally from her rough "handling" his neck started to heavily bleed again. at that point i lost it! the other nurse k. said she didn't like my "tone" and left. my husband was in a horrendous condition and i was supposed to bow and whisper? the manager rachel rushed in to yell at me and defend her nurses of course. it was like spanish inquisition. "we are going to call security" became their signature dish. instead of me sitting and comforting my husband, i was on high alert non-stop and he had to witness me fighting neglect for months. besides physical pain and cancer, he was going through emotional agony watching me stand against the tsunami alone. 

on the day of my husband's passing we had a day shift nurse emily g. whenever she was our nurse she was always sweet, patient and caring. day shift sicu is the reason i will never use medical city dallas,i rather die in the streets. same goes for all our friends, family, colleagues, neighbors, their friends and families, it's spreading like wildfire, everyone is blown away. my husband was my life, my air, my light. half of me died when my love took his last breath, the other half of me is crippled. i will remember every nurse till i stop breathing and i know i will meet them all at the gates of hell one day.
