my review on google 2 months ago was deleted. here it is copy and pasted, also edited a bit.
i was a patient at harbor oaks hospital many times in the adolescent (pediatric) section. your personal freedom here is pretty much deprived, as it is in most places. you have limited access to your clothes, hygiene material, books, anything used to help or regulate yourself. try to bring pg books, they won't be hesitant to take away any 'graphic' material (non-gut-churning material such as stephen king is not allowed, neither are books on psychology/mental health, or books with tragedy (drug addiction, mental health crisis, suicide, etc) as it is assumed other patients will read your materials. if lucky, the nurses/behavioral techs will take pity on your situation and let you have some of your 'graphic' books and the like. 
anyway, harbor oaks. not the best hospital. treatment is less than mediocre or adequate. no interacting with the opposite sex, which i can understand, although they don't stop children from butting into a situation such as phone calls, a personal matter with the nurses/behavioral techs, or whatever. children, if not enough beds on their side, will be housed on the teen girls' side. not the best choice. they will put transgenders on whichever side their sex at birth is. no lgbt rights whatsoever yet they won't stop patients from telling you graphic details of their sexual assault/abuse. being abused is a horrible thing and to be dealing with that, and have someone whom you've first met tell you their graphic details of abuse, is not something i enjoyed, and i wouldn't expect anyone to enjoy this either. the interaction with the same sex is not monitored. 
the food is not terrible, although what they promise for dinner is the opposite you receive. for example, if they promise cookies/cake/brownies, you may get gelatin or something of that sort. 
the social worker, eva, is inadequate and treats her adolescent patients like they are children. there are groups 2-4 times a day, and you will be frequently bored, no matter what they tell you. there is rarely treatment that addresses destructive behaviors or any other disorder besides clinical depression/persistent depressive disorder. if that is your issue, go to this hospital. if you struggle with something more complex, such as childhood abuse, destructive behaviors, eating disorders, personality disorders, etcetera, spend your money someplace else. 
they'll dope you up to as far as 600 m.g, morphing you into a zombie. you get no say in your aftercare or treatment in general. 
the average stay here, from what i remember, is 5-9 days. sometimes longer, sometimes shorter. the shortest i saw someone stay was 3-4 days, the longest, 13. it depends on your behavior and why you're there in the first place. 
the psychiatrist, dr. sanjeev venkataraman, (dr. raman, for short) can be pretty empty and fail to explain why you need a certain medication or give you an estimate for your discharge date. like most treatment facilities, more often than not, you will gain weight. the staff and psychiatrists will not care; you will be punished for not eating. 
your discharge date will likely be on a weekday. the psychiatrists rarely work on weekends. 
the groups range from rec. therapy (walking/exercising mindlessly in the adult gym for about an hour, making bracelets), and others. i cannot recall, as they were unimportant then and still unimportant now as i fail to remember them or their contents. 
the majority of adolescents were there for suicidal ideation. i wouldn't recommend sending your adolescent child here for substance abuse, as i recall, you are unable to mention anything related to addiction whatsoever. send them to a therapist. teen rehabs are disgusting and used for clout.
i don't know if harbor oaks made me worse in terms of suicidal ideation and destructive behaviors, though i know because of this facility and others, i've gained weight. this has sent my self-esteem to an all-time low. 
there have been reports of child abuse throughout this facility. i never saw or heard of anything like that whilst i was there multiple times. only after it'd been months after i left the most recent time i'd been there did i hear about a young child being slammed to the floor and getting a concussion. 
visitation times are, from what i recall, 3-5 times a week. phone calls twice a day, ten minutes. parents choose your contact list. only immediate family. 
as i mentioned you get no say in your aftercare and will likely be sent to a new oakland face to face location. this program, in particular, is pretty gross and please advocate for your rights. tell your parents not to send you. 
try to talk to your child before sending them away. sending them to a treatment facility such as harbor oaks may make them worse. do your research, don't believe everything you hear.

doc_text:
nothing in life is more irritating than when a billing dept. contacts you with a price that is significantly lower than the price presented to you from your healthcare insurance provider.  

prior to being rendering services at this location, i was contacted by billing and was presented with the amount of $738.72 as well as a request for payment.  mind you, this is before being rendered services; hence my insurance had not yet been billed.  aggravating, i know.

then, when i go check in, the same amount was listed in their system; and then after being rendered services, an estimate w/ that same amount was sent to me via usps; with a request for payment.  

meanwhile, i decided to go and check my claim through my healthcare insurance provider and i see an amount of $1,684 for the same services; as the amount of my deductible.  i call my insurance and inform them that i was presented with an amount that was less than 50% than the amount displayed on their portal; only to be told that that is the accurate amount that i will be responsible for.  so what happens next, you ask...

i file a grievance through my healthcare insurance and then contact the attorney general's office; even though i know deep down inside that not a damn thing is going to change what has happened.  i wait to hear back from either or; and below and behold i hear back from my healthcare insurance provider with the lame explanation of:  " in review of your grievance, i brought your case to the attention of a svh patient access operations director, who appreciated being made aware of your concern. the director stated that you were provided an estimate based off the cpt code that was going to be used during the procedure. the director stated that the estimate is subject to change if the provider in question uses a different service code (cpt code) or adds any services..."  

ok...let me start off by saying... that in the world of business, i have witnessed estimates being different by either 10-20%... and the differential is usually written on the estimate to let the customer know.  
in this case, the amount was over a 50% difference and nowhere was it listed that the amount could be significantly higher... also too, where it was an "estimate" then they truly had no flippin' business requesting payment in the first place.

seriously... the poor business displayed by the billing department is unbelievable and the fact that they can get away with, what other companies cannot, is repulsive.  i mean,  would you allow a company to bill you a price that is significantly higher than the price you were originally presented with?  would they not have to honor that lower price?

i thought so... 

so with all due respect, what makes this situation any different?  it may be the medical field, but it's still a business...and well the same rules should still have to apply... 

needless to say... i am not in the least bit impressed and if i have my way, i will be taking my medical needs elsewhere in the future.

this review is for the dental department!

va dental is much harder to qualify for than medical. if you're 100% disabled, then you're in there and it's free. such a blessing! 

cons: my only complaint is that i have to go to la jolla. there isn't a dental facility at the mission valley location, which sucks for people like me who live in otay (near aquatica). this can mean 1-1.5 hour commute in the morning. but again, it's free, so i'm definitely making the drive. 

i'm new to va dental (as of january 2020) and have had the absolute best experience so far. i called to set my initial intake appointment and they were booked out six months so my appointment would be in june 2020. i thought that was insane, but the truth is that people call in and cancel their appointments everyday. don't let this discourage you! let me explain...

i had a dental emergency and the front desk staff instructed me to come into their walk-in clinic that opens at 0800 i believe. she told me to check in at 0730 and i'd be the first seen. i did that and it turned out that i had an infection from a year old root canal. they put me on antibiotics and scheduled me with their top endodontist, dr. sulter!  i am such a baby when it comes to procedures, even shots! i literally l got sick before the appointment just getting nervous about it. dr. sulter and her assistant were fantastic! they have been there together for 10 years. they were extremely concerned about my comfort and did everything possible to ease my worries. they were extremely gentle too...i didn't feel the shots! i found out that i have extremely long roots that a previous dentist didn't clean correctly. she prescribed me a stronger antibiotic due to what she found and some yeast infection medicine due to the antibiotic side effects on me. this is the first dentist to do this for me!!

i had another tooth that was a bootcamp root canal that was never crowned and finally crack to the point of missing half the tooth. she took it upon herself to schedule me the following week to take care of it. she also referred and authorized me to see an amazing dentist out in town because i need a special procedure done on one tooth. i also told her about my front tooth that had been bothering me.  i cracked my tooth on deployment and the good ol navy dental covered it up with a yellow color while my teeth are extremely white. it's so embarrassing! she referred me to dr. henz, who personally called me the next day.

dr.  henz was able to schedule me in for my intake appointment first, which meant i didn't have to wait til june. when i tell you guys...the most thorough dental exam ever! her assistant was awesome too even though he's a vikings fan, go bears! in the same week, she scheduled me for impressions on one of my root canals for a crown. the other needs a crown lengthening procedure that they had to send me out in town for. i've already seen that dentist as well and will have the procedure done next week with a month of healing time. 

on the same day as my intake appointment, i went to the front desk to schedule a cleaning. they told me it wouldn't be til september (keep in mind, it's now january). what can i do? another lady  told her to wait because she was sure there was a cancellation in march. then another lady said she was cancelling an appointment that same day in about 30 minutes and asked if i'd like to take it....uhhh absolutely! the front desk staff are awesome and they really work together!

i got my teeth cleaned by oscar i believe and he did an amazing job. the best part about him, dr. sulter, and dr. henz is that they all walked me through the process and educated me about cleaning my teeth properly, recommended products, and gave tips on maintaining my wisdoms. i have all of my adult teeth and this is the only dental facility that didn't try to have me wisdoms removed due to possible "hygiene" problems or telling me i'd get crooked teeth, mine are straight! 

all of this happened during the month of january! if you be need to get in sooner, you can! you have to call up there though...cancellations happen all the time and the staff encourage you to call them and check.

don't be discouraged by someone's horror story of navy dental, the va has the latest technology and new or not,  their staff is educated!

for disabled veteran's the vamc is a great choice as it is free based on your combined disability rating. what many veteran's do not know is that if you have over a 30% medical disability rating you qualify for "free" medical insurance through the va. i fall into this category and i have always been taken care of, but you have to be patient. this is such a busy medical center and san diego is a major hub for veterans that you often have to wait 3-4 weeks for any appointment made. did this reason i also pay for private medical insurance through my work. i find this to be very beneficial because my private health care provider can get my seen quickly and diagnosed. based on the diagnosis (cost of treatment) i schedule the my surgeries and procedures through them at no cost to myself. 

my suggestion for those who qualify for the free medical insurance is to get enrolled asap. it takes some time to get the process started and to get an established va health care primary provider so get to work! this coverage pays off, but be proactive and get enrolled prior to needing urgent medical attention. following the approval process and referral process can be very time consuming and annoying so if it is within your budget carry dual coverage (private). use the medical notes from your private provider to skip levels and expatiate the va medical process. 

overall i have to give the service a 4 star rating. i love that they take care of veterans and i have seen improvements every year.

surprised to see all the negative reviews here--so i'll preface this by saying my experience was with the er department specifically. 

went on a thursday morning and the check-in was relatively quick. thank you, whitney! i fainted after they drew blood (whoops), and one of the phlebotomists went to find somewhere for me to lay down (thanks, stuart) while the other held my hand and wiped the cold sweat off my face. thank you, anne, i was really touched by your kindness and reassurance.

thank you also odessa, david, and the brazilian (?) gentleman with the lapis lazuli bracelet whose name i didn't catch because i was still woozy from the blood draw. and jason (?) for the ct scan and the experience of being injected with contrast, which i was told would feel like peeing myself but actually felt like drinking butterbeer ^w^

not sure if i got lucky, if it's the er department in particular, or if the reviews here swing negative because--let's be honest--a lot of patients are in highly stressful and emotional situations when they write these, but i got good vibes from this place. 

in fact, i overheard some conversations between coworkers (my room was by some kinda reception desk), and from what i can deduce, it sounds like they have a healthy workplace culture where the staff is genuinely invested in the wellbeing of their colleagues + patients & quality of their work. 

a rare thing when modern western medicine is characterized by uncaring, clinical coldness.

keep doing what you do, er team!

p.s. regarding all these reviews about payment problems...the fault typically lies with your insurance and not the healthcare provider. over the past decade+, patients have been forced to shoulder more and more of the burden of healthcare bills because insurance companies are covering less and less. medical billing & collections is an ugggggly thing, and the heinous greed of for-profit insurance corps is to blame.

i wish i had the time to really explain my experience at henry mayo.  in july, i had a bad kidney infection and went against my gut instinct to go to cedars, and opted to go to henry mayo because it is closer.  i should have followed my gut instinct.  

their website said that the er had a five-minute wait.  

i was in the er for eight hours without a room, just stuck on a gurney in the hallway with no pain medicine (i was in excruciating pain), no care whatsoever, and had to be moved to another hallway at one point due to some loud and crazy criminal who was threatening patients (cops were everywhere).  it was a nightmare.

finally i was put into a room, and received pain medicine.  the nurses felt really bad for me, and that was appreciated.  the room was shared (unnecessary as they had many empty rooms) and my roommate wanted the room so hot i was dripping sweat.  the nurses called the room "the sauna" because it was so hot in there.  i begged them to turn down the temperature and every time they tried, she'd cry and beg them to turn it up because she was so cold (even with many blankets).  i am not a complainer, and not demanding in the slightest. she was very loud and very demanding.  so she won out.  they could have moved me into another room--that would have been great.  but no.  it was days of this...it was awful.  finally, i was ready to go home and because they didn't have the proper staff to release me (it was a friday and they are understaffed on the weekends), they wanted me to stay an extra 2.5 days because they would be back on monday.  

i could not deal with this for that long--besides, i did not want to overcharge my insurance company (that seemed like fraud to me), so i checked myself out ama.  they threatened that my insurance would not pay (this is blatantly not true).  they tried everything to scare me into staying.  my doctor even told me to go home.  they refused to talk to me once i signed on the dotted line, and would not even give me outprocessing papers.  i had to walk myself to my car.  fine with me.  the nurses were really pissed.  i found out later that they are audited based on number of amas, and they get dinged for each one.  i'm sorry for that, but maybe they should run a better business.

top all of that off with receiving a $1500 bill from the er doc--the doc i never saw.  turns out that, though the hospital is in my network, they hire out of network doctors for their er.  now i'm fighting with my insurance company, the doctor, and the hospital.  this is ridiculous.  this has happened to me before--getting an out of network doc in an er--and now i always ask if the doc is in my network.  if not, i won't see them and/or i'll go to another er.  i did this on this trip, and was told that he was in my network.  they lied.  he is not.  this is quite a racket, henry mayo--taking the people who need the care the most, who put their trust in you, and give them the bait-and-switch with out-of-network doctors who will bill as much as they want for their "care" (even if there is no care).

between the misleading information on their website for er wait times, the lack of care in the er, the hospital experience, ama experience, and final billing--this was a nightmare that i hope i can save you from.  skip it.  it's just not worth the convenience of "local".  

providence holy cross is not far from here--and it's a great hospital.  next time in the need of an er, i'll either go there or to cedars.  never again, henry mayo.

this is regarding the er. i was incredibly disappointed with the care received. my little sister fainted while in the shower during her period. she had a small gash on her head-- because it was on her face we wanted to make sure there was no scarring and thus took her to the er. when we got there, they checked us in... and called us to the back for an ekg and blood work (excessive, yes, but it is the er). they took us back to the front, and called us back again for a chest x-ray. the np was walking by so we inquired as to why a chest x-ray was needed for someone who fainted (with known cause) after an ekg was already done.  the np proceeded to tell us that football players have fainted and died (completely irrelevant). i asked her if the ekg was normal, and her response was that there was syncope and we needed to find the cause of the syncope. then she asked my 18 yr old sister if she felt a vagal response. i looked up what syncope was on my phone- "fainting"? why is a medical professional using these terms when talking to patients? terrible bedside manner. my sister had to ask what she meant, and she still was unable to explain properly. i asked if my sister needed all these tests as she has been acting completely normal- she just has a cut on her forehead and i wasn't sure if it'd scar. np asked when the fall occured and i told her it was 10 am (this was about 11 hours later), and she responded she didn't realize. i asked if they would give my sister treatment without all these diagnostics tests and the np said that they would not! we felt stuck at that point, because the stitches needed to be done within a certain time frame. after all of this, we to the front and get called back again-they decided to finally take vitals/check the blood pressure of the girl who fainted! they also said they needed to take do a cat scan of her head! at this point, we refused treatment to the tech and said we needed to see an md/physician. the ct tech said okay and said we could go back out front. over an hour later, we were called back so more blood could be drawn; i asked if there was something wrong with the first draw, and was told no- they simply have to draw blood for the particular test over a period of six hours. we inquired as to why this was necessary and where the doctor was and why this was all needed for some stitches! the np came and said she was waiting on the cat scan results before she did stitches. we asked her who was ordering all these tests, and we absolutely refuse to have a cat scan. she said the doctor ordered them and we'd have to sign a waiver saying we decline treatment. we said we would like to see the doctor who is ordering these tests, because why is he/she doing so without even seeing the patient. she said she was ordering on behalf of the doctor. we proceeded to sternly say we need to see a doctor, and her response was, "well i see patients all the time by myself." we replied that was fine but we need to see a doctor. in the meantime, she went back to her office and we heard her talking to the doctor on speakerphone who said that we did not need to sign anything, but simply make sure it was noted in the chart. after some time we were put in a room, and then waited for the doctor. 
the poor doctor came in a while later and was very sweet. i was ready to just have my sister receive treatment and leave, but my mother said it was important to tell/ask about what happened because other patients need protection to. i then went into detail of everything happened, and said i felt the chest x-ray was completely unnecessary, i was appalled that the blood pressure of a patient who came in because she fainted was taken after having a chest x ray, and the bedside manner and advanced terminology of the np (kim tarver) was unacceptable. very surprisingly, the doctor agreed. she professionally stated she agreed that the chest xray was unnecessary and my sister did not need a cat scan. she said the blood pressure thing was an outlier, but still needed to be noted...and she stated the terminology used was a personnel issue. after all this, she used liquid stitches (liquid skin) on my sister. she's good to go now, but it was an incredibly painful, unnecessary process.

aurora behavioral health center has a very inviting website, yet it's not what it seems.
my friend checked in to detox from an alcohol binge and only needed to safely detox so went in to do an intake process. once she signed some paper work she was then removed most of her belongings only leaving her in jeans and a long sleeve shirt. 
she was brought up to her ward and was given very little direction aside from where her room was and where the schedule for the day was on the wall. because it was 5pm they provided no food for her because dinner had already taken place at 4:30.
during her first night she became concerned and spoke with the nurse about the chances of leaving and doing an intensive out patient program instead. they told her this isnt how it works and she would be there as long as the psychiatrist saw fit. 
she asked if there was any way to leave legally and the nurse reluctantly said that there was an option of an ama (against medical advice) but that they highly discouraged it and that her insurance probably wouldn't cover it and that she would still have to stay a mandatory 24 hours after signing it.  this is a way to deter you from leaving as there are several homeless addicts in the hospital as well.
this was only for detox from only alcohol, not even hard alcohol. she wasn't depressed, suicidal and only expressed that she had some anxiety.
she was finally able to call me the next day when they opened up the phones. this is when she told me the ward was really cold and uncomfortable, probably around  60-65 degrees.  the beds are were hard and had a sheet and a very thin blanket with a plastic pillow. she said it was almost impossible to stay warm considering she only had a shirt on. they gave her a hospital town to keep her extra warm.  the social room was also very uncomfortable, very hard furniture. pretty much the most uncomfortable setting she could have wanted for help.  the whole process is very systematic, you are treated as a prisoner, the only plus side is they give you drugs so you can sleep.
while she was there she met several people that had only gone in there to speak to a therapist or get counseling cause they felt depressed and they were stuck there over a week. constantly told they couldn't leave because the psychiatrist didn't feel that they were ready. these were people that didn't walk in even on medication!  they ended up prescribing my friends with three prescriptions when really she only wanted to safely detox from alcohol.
this is a scary process and if you dont have insurance they wont let you discharge without paying in full. this is why they keep you as long as possible.

just so people know. you shouldn't be discouraged to sign an ama is you feel like the treatment isn't helpful. you can also call the police to come get you if you want to leave.

i know people need help but this really wrecked my friend, not just for her but for her family.  she also mentioned there's no one on one therapy, they do group sessions that most people walk out of and they are directed by inexperienced social workers. most the time the more talkative patients take over the group and it ends up pointless.

i can't believe anyone would recommend this place for someone that isn't categorized as smi (severe mental issues).

oh god, she's so fat

ok lets be straight- i'm a big girl. i've struggled with my weight my whole life. 
i'm also narcoleptic, and have fought a battle with depression and anxiety since i was 10. are these things an issue? yep. do they define me and explain every issue without an obvious answer? no, they do not. 

unless, of course, i am an in-patient at abrazo central campus.

the first doctor i met was called "dr. d." the first thing to roll out of his mouth upon meeting me was "have you considered gastric bypass surgery?" no hello? the second thing was "are you diabetic?" diabetes was a natural first question, as i was there because neuropathy in my feet was spreading alarmingly fast up both my legs.

something to rule out for sure, but folks, i am not diabetic. 

not if abrazo staff pokes me every 6 hrs for 2 days, not if the dr orders 2 different blood tests, not if he adds insulin to my prn list while neglecting my actual prescriptions, not by the hair of my chinny chin chin! 
so whats next?

oh awesome, here comes the neurologist. a gallon or two of my blood was taken for testing, a spinal tap and mri were ordered. 

the spinal tap was, of course, terrifying. one of my symptoms was spontaneous involuntary muscle spasms and they wanted to put a giant needle in my spine that could paralyze me if i moved! 
i had a panic attack. i have already admitted that i have anxiety. but wouldn't you call that a reasonable fear? 

now, looking over the paperwork, i see references to my anxiety all over the place as a poor explanation for their failure to find the reason for the neuropathy

but back to the fat prejudice, as that is my theme.
 
when i was admitted, i was starving. i had spent hours in the er before being transferred to the hospital. i had only expected to spend a few hours at the er and for them to do whatever they do and send me home.
so i asked for a sandwich. 3 hours and multiple ignored requests passed between me and that sandwich. it was one of those little elementary school sized ones with one slice of mystery meat, a slice of cheese, and two pieces of bread cut in a diagonal. 

i ate it thankfully. an hour later, i was still hungry and asked if there was somewhere i could get some food. perhaps a vending machine? they put me off a couple more hours and served me fat shame with my second sandwich. 

then, when i was sitting up in bed in the middle of the night (as i do multiple times a night, part of the narcolepsy) the nurse walking by stopped and asked, "your not eating again, are you?" with a horrified expression on his face. 

time for the mri came, and the tech walked in, looked at me, and walked back out into the hall. he announced that i was too fat for the machine several times using different descriptors. he was ordered to try anyways. yep, i heard all of it. i'm sure the neighboring rooms did too. 

he left, and came back with the biggest wheelchair i have ever seen. 
i told him i had heard him in the hall, and he did look genuinely embarrassed and apologetic, so i dropped it.  it turns out that i did fit, but it was so snug that we decided it would be better to wait for a machine that was 70 inches rather than the one there that was 60. 

so yeah, he was pretty much right. 

but my complaint is about a complete and widespread attitude of prejudice and lack of tact because of my weight. 

i am also concerned about the fact that we, the patients, could hear everything the staff was saying to each other in the hallway. i can tell you exactly what was wrong with the people on either side of me and not because i was trying to listen. i think its unprofessional. 

i have a lot of other complaints too.... but i'll just leave it at that.

well, that and that my symptoms have not resolved, an explanation has not been found, and now i have a giant bill for labs that nobody bothered to interpret, and that i can only pray the insurance company will cover most of. 
the list is a few pages long. i may have been tested for bubonic plague, i haven't made it through the whole list yet.

if you are planning a visit to an abrazo er, do a quick check first. can you see your feet while standing up? 

if not, you might want to chose a different er.

this review is for the walk-in/urgent care clinic. i was told at the ward clinic the wait would be 45 minutes there so i called here and the receptionist said that she couldn't promise anything but at the moment there was only one patient and two doctors. i was in a bit of pain so decided to come here instead. 

i wasn't aware the main hospital had a walk-in clinic, but the receptionist at ward was very helpful in explaining where to find it, and that we should park in the main hospital garage.

so fyi, the walk-in clinic is in the strode building to the right as you're looking at the entrance from king street. my husband dropped me off at the patient dropoff area so that i could go to the clinic while he parked, and there were plentiful signs for the strode building. it's located just past the pharmacy, and you go through a walkway to get to it. 

the super helpful receptionist quickly took my info and immediately provided me with a cup for a urine sample. i provided it, and it took about 10-15 minutes before they called me back to see the doctor.

based on previous experience, i thought it was a kidney infection or kidney stone - but i wanted to rule out appendicitis because two of my sisters had to have surgery for it, one of them just a month ago.

after hearing my symptoms, dr. susie chun didn't think it was appendicitis and ordered an ultrasound to check my right kidney, where the pain was. we then went to radiology, which is in the main building, second floor. the receptionist and techs were also friendly and helpful there; btw it's super freezing in there, so they provide warm blankets in a metal heater at the back, against the wall. note: you open the heater by pulling on the right side of the door, not the left. watched a couple of people struggle to open it before realizing what side to open. also, for an ultrasound, you must have a full bladder. because i emptied mine to provide a sample at intake, i had to drink several cups and wait about 20 minutes before they could do the procedure.

after the ultrasound, we went back to the clinic, where dr. chun said it showed slight inflammation to my kidney. she didn't want to have me go straight to a ct scan since it involves radiation, but with the ultrasound results she thought it best to confirm with a ct scan. so i went back to radiology, where they were just as nice the second time, and did the procedure quickly.

back at the clinic again, and dr. chun confirmed the kidney stone, showing me the imaging of one in my kidney (wasn't causing the pain) and one in my ureter (that was the culprit). it wasn't large enough to require surgery so she prescribed a medication to help me pass that sucker and i could go home. all in all it took about three hours, but the pain had eased and i was so relieved,  i could be patient with all the tests. 

everyone at both clinics were so helpful and friendly, from the receptionists to the nurses to dr. chun. it was a fairly slow saturday so maybe that made for a better experience since no one was rushed dealing with a ton of patients, but i appreciated the warmth and care i received today. it made a very uncomfortable experience much easier to bear.

i tried to address the issues with sutter twice, but their response was that they didn't know much about le or the le clinic or what the pts did, so there you go. i even asked if i could feel out a patient survey -- nope. 

i then ordered this pt's assessment and clinical progress notes** from our every appointment. omg! not only did this pt write down inaccurate information, but she.....was less than truthful. for example, appointments were scheduled for 75 minutes each. except for a few exceptions, my appointments were only 60 minutes long! she was chronically late (by 15 - 20 minutes) for every appointment, but one. how do i know this? because i also documented our appts! and what kinds of things did she write?  she wrote that our appointments were a full 75 minutes. bs! i was shortchanged in one way or another for every appointment.

worst er experience ever! do not let them fast track you in the er! this is a review of my er department experience. i had to be wheeled in with a wheelchair because i could not walk at all. i reported that i fell and had knee, back and hip pain. i feared i had broken something. i was in horrible pain and reported i was uncomfortable in a seated position. when the triage nurse said she was going to put me in "fast track", i thought that would be a good thing. it is not! turns out fast track is a minor emergency triage option. very appropriate for kids with ear infections, etc. but not for trauma!!! they wheeled me to a tiny hot waiting room where we waited for an hour and a half only to be directed to a room the size of a regular er room with 5 or 6 recliners separated by curtains. the room was tiny and also very hot. i told the nurse i could not sit in that chair, that i needed a bed. sitting in the wheelchair for as long as i had had caused my pain to increase a lot! they said they don't have a bed. sorry. i explained my pain and injury and they said that's all they have. so they put me in a torn up recliner(they were all torn up) that had a broken handle and didn't even recline. i was in tears by this point. the pa had another patient change seats with me because mine didn't recline. after a while of sitting in pain and crying the pa saw me, after she saw another kid with an ear infection. i happen to know every symptom and treatment for every other person in that room because, remember, only curtains separated the many chairs. another fun point, we got the chair directly beside a very dirty bathroom with no soap that apparently was the only one for the whole er department, because the traffic level was very high. my wife was constantly stepping out of the bathroom seekers way. imagine being examined by the pa while tons of little kids brushed past to get to the bathroom. of course they stopped and watched for a bit because they are kids and they don't understand how horribly inappropriate that is. the pa promised pain meds soon, but no one came. i was taken to the xray room with no pain meds and i cried and cried through the whole xray. my pain was at a 10 and i had to climb around on that hard cold xray table. well at least the table was cold after sitting in the 100 degree fast track waiting room and joke of an er room. they finally came with some meds. pills, no iv's here! no pillows for my knee to at least try to make me more comfortable. nothing. nothing but a bunch of kids with ear infections. 
we begged them to move us to a room. we asked 2 nurses and the pa and they all said, "i'll see what i can do". i bet you can guess what they did. nothing. there was a young man that also was in the fast track waiting room with us, and i saw the room across the hall from us empty and they put him in it because the recliners were all full. instead of moving me into the room and putting him in the recliner that he was apparently in line for too. are you kidding me!!?? 
look- i think that fast track deal has its place and is a good idea....for kids with ear infections!!!! not for a trauma patient in extreme pain. if i was mobile enough i would have left and gone somewhere else. but guess what? they took my wheelchair, so i couldn't go anywhere. not even to the bathroom. my wife had to help me hop to the bathroom when i couldn't wait any longer. i'll tell you this is the absolute worst er experience i have ever had in all of my 50 years. no bed, no iv, no pillow or blanket, no m.d. and no empathy either. unless you are bringing in a kid with an earache, do not let them put you in that "fast track" it is an absolute joke. in fairness, i had treatment at that er on a previous occasion and had a regular er room, and dr. jordan was wonderful. i was not so lucky this time. summary: i did not receive appropriate treatment for my specific need. i was ignored. the staff was rude.

from the beginning, the er doctors misevaluated my father's medical condition.  first doctor said, he had a small puka in his lung, that could be  why for his shortness of breath; it turned out to be a shadow that they mistaken it for on the x-ray.  second, another doctor or nurse said he might have an bleeding ulcer, cause blood was found in the stool; it turned out to be not as bad, just a tiny bit which could be residue from a recent bleeding ulcer.  third, another doctor said, he has a slight collasped lung, which could be the reason for shortness of breath.  all this caused a roller coaster of emotions for me because he was weak as it is. they said he was going to be moved upstairs in-house for few days, but we waited hours & hours, and still no move.  i finally asked the nurse, then got an overall negative answer that the er is so full & in-house there's no room, so he eventually was placed in an narrow hallway at the er for hours again.  he was supposed to be discharged at 3:30 pm. at the time it was around 11:15 am.
we wanted to check if everything went okay with the transporting, but found out that he didn't leave until much later!   my dad is 99 yrs old, imagine being left there in the hallway for hours.  i'm hoping they gave him lunch (probably not) cause how in the world can he eat in a narrow hallway with no hospital table!!  i'm also hoping they've been changing his adult diapers!!! probably not, cause even while we were there, the nurse only changed him twice!  if you have an elderly parent, they need to be checked if they soiled their diapers like a baby.  i know this is not a care home but they're not considering problems that could occur if my father is left to himself!   why couldn't they send people to another hospital if there are no room.  i feel like the doctors just needed a reason/justification for tending to my dad so that they get paid by insurance.
i hate saying that, but why all the medical reasoning and later re-track from it?!  in the end, he's the same as he came in.  it was a waste of time and money sending him there.

my suggestion - don't go to queen's hospital er----they're just too busy!!!

thank you, swedish hospital!

if you are having surgery, like i did here,  remember to address your fears if u have a special circumstance like if most people have a pair of 2 organs but you only have 1, and they removing giant growths from it, but they've already told you that if it bleeds, they must remove it. because they can totally forget. in my case i could've become castrated if they removed my ovary, because i only had 1 left. then i would've been thrust into menopause and my life would've shortened abruptly and thrust into rapid aging.

everything was a success. i'm fine now.

my 92-year old grandfather was admitted directly from st.jude er due to insurance reasons on 12/30/19. it is definitely not one of the nicer hospitals. but i do think the staff here does an amazing job, the nurses in particular. he initially got admitted to dou in the middle of the night, during which grace (almost positive that was her name) was the admitting nurse. i was not present but i was on the phone with her during the entire intake process since my parents speak minimal english. i could clearly tell she was incredibly patient and caring, thoroughly explaining every level of dnr and expressing her concern for blood in his urine seen in the foley bag. she ensured that his pain was controlled from the foley insertion (which was immense), not treating him like a drug seeking patient. 

the next day he was transferred to med-surg 3rd floor, stella (daytime) as his nurse for the next 2 days. she likewise provided exceptional service, tending to all his/our needs in a very prompt manner. she consistently went above and beyond, not hesitating to call physicians and inpatient pharmacy to obtain orders, inquire about starting his new chemo meds, verifying home meds, etc. 

the last nurse i encountered was chona up until his discharge (1/4). i did not have too much interaction with her but according to my sister, she was also very kind to make sure that he was able to be discharged home with enough supplies before home health nurse can visit. 

shift manager (unfortunately don't remember her name) was also diligent in consulting case management when we expressed our concern for discharging without having a follow-up with a urologist and oncologist, given he newly had a foley catheter and a nephrostomy tube, although the doctors were basically telling him to just follow up with the primary doctor to get referred to a urologist. i knew for a fact that it often takes months to  see a specialist through primary md referral. case management did an amazing job of securing an appointment with an oncologist, urologist, and even home health within a day. thanks to them we were able to take him home, knowing he will have adequate follow up with the doctors and professional care for his foley and nephrostomy tube dressing changes at home. 

we were less impressed by the physicians but everyone else sort of made up for it. maybe it's because i'm an inpatient pharmacist and knew to demand the right things to the right people, but they really did deliver. and even though i deal with nurses everyday, being on the other side as  patient's family, i realized so much respect and gratitude for all the nurses who genuinely care for their patients.

that has significantly altered my cognitive ability. unfortunately, it has caused me to forget some of the names of a few of the remarkably compassionate, funny, kind, competent medical professionals i have ever had the privilege to be cared for by. but it has truly been the nurses and nursing assistants who have saved me here. over the last nearly 4 years, i have lost the love of my life, two close friends, a cousin i grew up with and my dear little dog. i came here angry and tearful and hopeless. i actually expected to wake up from surgery missing a leg. so, here goes. the nurses...lizzy, i was in coastal harbor treatment center for 2 weeks, from 12.13.2019 to 12.27.2019. i was in the residential 2 east girls' unit for self-harm. i was supposed to stay for half a year, but my "treatment team" decided to release me after 2 weeks because i believe they thought i was violent or self-harmed but in fact, i was not. the reason i was sent there, according to my mom, was refusal to take my medication and because i had a "bad attitude". i have anxiety, depression, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, tourette's syndrome, and adhd, but i am not physically aggressive and i have no history of self-harm, despite what my mother says (she says she stopped me from self-harming, when in fact i stopped her from self-harming)

when i was there, i had a very mediocre experience. 

when you first arrived, you were on "precautions" for up to 10 days, i was on it for about 9. this meant you could not do any fun activities like recreational therapy and you ate meals on the unit. you could also not have any pencils or pens. this is nearly also the case if you get what they called a "privilege freeze", where they gave you no privileges for 7 days, freeze was supposed to be for kids who were physically aggressive or self harmed but they instead gave them out because kids either talked to staff in a tone they didn't like or didn't get out of the shower quick enough. i got a freeze for talking to a staff member about a complaint i had with the program. said complaint was that we actually did nothing worthy of treatment. all we did was watch movies. i never went outside during my entire stay because they told me there was a "runaway risk". i also got threatened with freeze 2 times; one time because i didn't get out of the shower fast enough and the other time because i was looking at the lunch menu "too long" during visitation time in the cafeteria.

i was originally in the 2 west unit for physical aggression, but i was moved to 2 east my first day there.

i had a full-on breakdown because i was scared and in an unfamiliar environment. i asked for a time-out, which they were supposed to give, but instead one of the mhts there, who's name was ms. g, pulled me by the neck and hair.

i complained of feeling sick and feeling like i was about to barf. i had no appetite the first few days i was there, yet the staff laughed at me for barely eating anything. all the nurses gave me for my nausea was a pill that didn't even help. i actually did throw up, but the staff made me clean my puke up with a rag despite me feeling sick and dizzy.

i was put in solitary for 1 hour because i said "what?" to a mht when i did not understand something that they said. i had a full-on breakdown in that solitary room and the mht who sent me there, i believe her name was ms. acia (ay-see-uh), did not do anything but scroll through her phone for that hour.

in terms of communication, it was actually very good. you got a 10-minute long uncensored phone call every night. you were allowed to send mail. they had visitation in the cafeteria every day which lasted for about an hour and 30 minutes and it was uncensored and very nice.

we did barely any treatment or groups. we had a "goals group" every morning, the only therapy group i could go to was once every weekday. the kids did recreational therapy (rt) every weekday but only people off of freeze and precautions were able to go. we had bible studies once a week, but luckily that was optional. the only thing we did all day, outside of school, was watch movies. on one sunday we watched 9 movies (i counted!). you met with your therapist twice a week, once for individual session and once for a family session.

we could not have any personal effects in our room. only clothes and a bible. and despite being non-denominational, we were required to say a christian prayer every morning.

education was very good. mr. jeff was my teacher, he had a good sense of humor and was a cool guy. learning was on odysseyware at our own pace. overall i say the education quality was nice and it was in a way that i liked.

an absolute horror show, travesty of medical care, and a lawsuit waiting to happen. 

my mom fell this week (fragile, dementia, history of stroke, and a hip replacement). i called 911 and on scene the paramedics asked which hospital we preferred- i chose mercy general as her pcp and records are all at dignity health. 

worst decision ever. 
how the hospital is run: 
a doctor saw my mom for a total of 1 minute at arrival and 30 seconds at exit. no supervision or accountability. lots of people here seemed "checked out" working in an untenable environment. 

medical assistants and one rn is on duty, one pa or doctor for what seemed to be 50 or more patients. there are lots of guys in green outfits doing, apparently, nothing that i noticed for the five hours we were there. my mom was parked on a gurney for the whole time in a busy hallway. people, patients, staff, gurneys, paramedics, security guards, and random people coming and going nonstop. 

she had imaging of her hip, elbow, and arm. there were good people doing the imaging. i repeated that her head hurt- mom chimed in- and then that was related to the doctor and a ct was ordered. too bad the doctor refused to talk to the patient and just felt  her bones for minute and didn't ask one question to her "patient" aka just a number.  props to the imaging team for maintaining a system and compassion for patients in a totally chaotic situation. 

she was offered a tylenol and glass of water. no updates on what was happening...i assumed a room would be provided eventually.  other patients parked in hallway, including a man and his wife- he begged to have someone help her use the restroom- for an hour. 

at about 8:30 pm the medical assistant popped by and said no broken bones, mom had to get up and prove she could walk before being released. i stepped in when mom got upright on the gurney and said she felt dizzy. 

medical assistant said she would have a chair behind mom as she walks. my dad was helping. honest to god, this was the plan. my mom fell, said she's dizzy, and they want her to walk in a busy hallway with people crashing around pell-mell. 

i spoke up loudly, said you need to get an orderly and she said, this is how we do it do you have a better suggestion? 

this could have been solved by having my mom move to a room- (literally across the hall an empty room with three hospital beds) for a safe environment for a trial run. 

we worked with situation at hand with me guarding the hall like a pit bull behind mom and blocking people and gurneys from coming through....and dad ready to catch mom. and then medical assistant tells mom to get back to 
the gurney after a successful trial run. mom has lymphedema and her swollen legs would be hitting metal. i said no get a wheelchair. then a guy in green shows up. apparently ready to catch mom if she falls. thanks, perfect timing. 

so, end of story- doctor comes by for 30 seconds to tell us no broken bones and runs off, totally masked  to protect herself from coronavirus. brava. medical assistant turned out to be a nice person and she stood by us while my dad got car. she was smart and empathetic once she was freed from caring for 50 people simultaneously with no tangible support. 

literally the worst er i have ever been in. train wreck, third world care. danger. no info. a few decent people trying to do their best in a disaster scene. never again. they should close their doors if they can't serve patients and provide a baseline of medical care. our east sac family has been born cared for. and died at mercy for three generations. sadly, switching care to sutter asap. 

every person who walks out of these doors should get a t-shirt that says, "i survived mercy er."

suggestion: hire some nuns to get this place shipshape. someone needs to be slapping a ruler.

brought my 5 year old son here last week not because he was experiencing cold symptoms but because he had also started wheezing when breathing and also vomiting. he had no fever but the wheezing concerned me because he has never had any issues with breathing or any asthma related issues. 
all the staff that helped were wonderful and friendly. 
they gave him some breathing treatments which really helped with the wheezing. they also did chest x-rays and tested for flu and strep. tests came back negative and x-rays looked fine. doctor said his lungs were reacting to something, possible allergy or asthma related, so he prescribed an asthma pump and a couple medications for nausea and his chest. 
came in at 3am, left around 7:30am. 

now almost a week later, my son woke up at 3:30am with a 104 fever that wouldn't go down. brought him in at 7:30am, was brought in immediately which was surprising to me because usually they make us wait a bit. doctor originally was going to just test again for flu because my boyfriend recently tested positive for it, and give him a bunch of fluids because his heart rate was out the roof. they also did some blood work. while we were waiting for results, he started screaming, crying, and clutching his stomach. this went on for 30 minutes before they were able to give him motrin which helped with the pain and fever. at this point i believe his temp was 102, heart rate still above 150. he also started vomiting a lot. now this concerned the doctor more also because his blood work showed his white blood cell count was 24 and normally should be 8-10. she said that was showing that his body is trying to fight something off so something was wrong. because he was clutching the  right side of his stomach, they thought it was possibly his appendix so he went off for an ultrasound. they couldn't see his appendix because his bladder was full and he did not want to pee so the result was that the doctor thought he might've had appendicitis and we were transferred to hartford hospital because it's a dedicated children's hospital and if it was appendicitis, he would have to have surgery to remove his appendix. waterbury hospital does not have a pediatric department. 
we were transferred about noon and got to hartford hospital about 12:30. 
once there we were seen immediately by a bunch of staff. he got an ultrasound done and appendix looked normal. they did more x-rays on him and turns out he had pneumonia (they could see it in the x-rays and doctor says it explains his fever, and abdominal pain). they diagnosed him in about an hour and a half, and we were out by 3. 
so....he had pneumonia since the first er trip we took but instead he was diagnosed with asthma and this second trip was diagnosed with possible appendicitis scaring me to death! why couldn't they see the pneumonia when they did the x-rays the first time from the very beginning?! extremely frustrating!!

still, the staff that helped me during this time were all great, friendly, and treated my son very well. 
i took 1 star off because of the wait time that always seems to be a problem and another star because of the improper diagnoses, not once but twice. 
i should've known though because when i came here for myself awhile back, they tested me for strep and although it came back negative, i was still prescribed strep medication for whatever reason. unbelievable! 
anyways, if you're coming here for your children, know they do not have a pediatric department so either go to saint mary's or i highly recommend hartford's children emergency department, worth the longer drive trust me!!!!

if you must seek out acute psychiatric care for your child, know that they will be well cared for at austin oaks.

i was sent here after being threatened by a brand new aprn who had no relevant experience in mental health issues and didn't bother to ask about safety plans or actual suicidal intent. she forcibly took away my actively tasking service animal, and threatened me with police action - which as a survivor of abuse resulted in me shutting down and dissociating.

while there i was given a prn anti-anxiety medication with known and severe possible interactions with my anti-depressants that could have caused significant medical issues. i was not given a suicide risk assessment until almost 48 hours later, despite the fact that it is required more frequently - the discharge paperwork was signed and dated before my only sra was completed.

i was strip-searched and threatened with violence for sighing. i was denied my own clothing back, and during the course of my stay, no fewer than three nurses and two male patients made inappropriate sexual comments about the clothing i was given. these nurses also ignored the information on my triggers and utilized specific phrasing that had been marked at intake as things to not say to me.

because my service animal was not present with me, i had a full autistic meltdown due to violations of my personal space, was frequently touched in areas that have nerve damage and are very painful for me to be touched at, and engaged in self-harmful stimming because i was not alerted to what i was doing so i could stop. i ended up with multiple additional scars on my arms from scratching at my skin (something which i do without noticing when i am overstimulated or stressed). no nurse or provider noticed or did anything to stop it, or provide first aid after the fact.

the group sessions were a load of hot garbage. they primarily focused on things which patients had no way of implementing, such as significant dietary changes or exercising out of doors. additionally, a lot of the information was significantly out of date or incorrect, such as claiming that depression can be caused by caffeine (there is no known link between the two), or that all carbohydrates make depression worse ( refined carbohydrates, such as white bread and soda, have been linked to depression in post-menopausal women, but unrefined carbs are not, and there's no known link between unrefined carbs and depression when eaten in a balanced diet). ironically, a majority of meals offered were high in processed sugars and refined carbs - deep-fried shrimp and preserved peaches, fried chicken tenders, sugary cereals, etc. as a person who needs to eat a fairly strictly balanced diet due to physical health issues, it made my overall health worse as well.

there were exposed cords in several areas, and the staff handling medication dispensation didn't pay attention to allergies. i have an anaphylactic reaction to ibuprofen, and was offered... ibuprofen for pain caused by a severely sprained ankle. if i had been actively suicidal i not only could have killed myself in this hospital, but would have been actively aided by the staff, since they openly admitted to not having any epipens or albuterol inhalants on site when i pointed out that they offered a medication that could kill me.

despite purportedly being a "voluntary" admission, i was denied the ability to check myself out, which is considered a felony charge for false imprisonment. i was threatened repeatedly with violence by the "therapist" present during a twenty minute meeting, and he lacked any relevant knowledge on autism, trauma, and comorbid issues which affected previous treatments i have received. he attempted to switch my anti-depressant to lexapro, ignoring the information provided in my medical charts which clearly state that lexapro was not an effective medication for my depression and that it had severe side-effects on me.

i was discharged after 48 hours, with no changes to my medication, no useful resources, three open wounds, and new additional trauma to add to my pile from being sexually harassed, threatened repeatedly with violence, being forcibly taken from my medical equipment, and being strip-searched.

unfortunately i cannot directly sue prairie st. john's for this because they have a disclaimer present on intake paperwork which i was coerced into signing, again under threat of violence. this is the last place anyone who needs any form of help should be sent to. they are a disgrace to the mental health field, and they have no appropriate oversight or checks in place to prevent medical malpractice or abuse of patients.

i had an accident last year where i lost my fingertip, it got caught in a door that the wind blew shut which removed the tip from the base of the fingernail. i went to this hospital, it was around midnight, and i had to wait 3 hours to see the doctor although no one appeared to be there. it was extremely painful and psychologically traumatic, yet the staff didn't seem very caring, and it took around 2 hours to get a shot for the excruciating pain. the shot was something called hydromorphone, formulated to not get people "high".
if ever there was a time a person needs to be a little bit high, it's when you have had a fingertip torn off. i have no history of drug abuse, though i understand we are all suspects due to the drug problem.
3 hours after i got there, i was given a shot in my hand which finally relieved the pain, if briefly, so the doctor could look at it and clean it up. after that a wonderful nurse wrapped it, and showed me how to do so which turned out to be a real blessing, as it had turned out my insurance had been cancelled shortly before though i didn't know, and i was not able to see a doctor afterwards because of that.

we should not be punished because of the drug issue, especially with a chopped off fingertip, the pain issue should have been addressed better. 
the 2 stars i do give was for the very nice nurse who bandaged my finger and showed me how to do it and what materials i needed.
i don't understand why i had to wait hours though when no one was there.
if i have an emergency again, i will try to have it taken care of in olympia instead if possible.

i take my hat off to the doctors, nurses, and staff at medstar washington hospital center because they are slammed with wall-to-wall patients, due to the recent shut-down of providence hospital and lack of hospitals in washington, dc, yet they still maintain a courteous and friendly demeanor. 

my family member just recently spent a week in this hospital and i can honestly say, it probably saved his limb. the doctors are so knowledgeable and aggressive with their diagnosis and willing to make rapid moves to save a life. we experienced nothing but patience and understanding towards the patient, as well as the family. the doctors/surgeons made time to discuss every option and outcome with the family and it was greatly appreciated. 

now i will say that the er triage is something like a third world country war zone. i've never been, but i can only imagine. since my family member was admitted to the hospital unexpectedly from a doctor's appointment, we were told that the er would be the easiest way to be admitted. whew! well, he was admitted easily, but the triage area was flooded with people!!! people stacked on top of people, no privacy, people in the hallways, cops guarding individuals that were under arrest...just a mass chaotic mess! people yelling out, hacking, sneezing, just a big germ fest. i wanted to go home and bathe in a bathtub filled with clorox and lysol. 

i truly didn't want to leave him there because he/everyone looked so miserable. it's no way on earth anyone could get any rest in this area because it's just a big ball of confusion. he spent two days in this confusion until he could get into a room. that's how crowded this hospital is, you have to wait until a room finally becomes available before you can leave the er. i don't know how they do it, but the nurses and doctors persevere on and act as if nothing is going on. i would lose my mind if i had to deal with this chaos everyday. 

oh how i wish dc would build a new hospital or 2 to take care of the citizens of the nation's capital!!! they need it asap!!!! 

after he was placed in a room, he was able to receive the care he so desperately needed.  if i was basing my review on the er alone, it would be a 1 star review, but since i had to factor in the staff, the rapid response of the doctors and my family member's care, i had to bring that star count up. this truly is a great hospital. it's just overcrowded. i truly hope another hospital can be built in the district to alleviate some of the crowds.

i'm sad to say that pmrc is more horrible than good which is why they get two stars from me on this review.

the bad

i am a stage 4 cancer survivor. unfortunately i end up at pmrc on a semi-regular basis for different cancer related problems. lets start with the doctors that work for the agency that is hired by the hospital who don't actually work for the hospital but instead float from hospital to hospital doing gods job. those specific doctors i believe went to "god school". now i'm not really sure if god school exists but if it does not then they attended a "god class" where they were all taught that they are gods! with their already inflated egos they behave as though they have a right to grant life or death with a swift hand. it was obvious to me that every doctor i had dealt with was of flesh and bones indicating to me that they do not walk side by side with god and therefore are not gods as they might try and make you believe. with my personality being the leader type, i have a tendency to butt heads with pompous over-inflated ego maniacs who think that they are my god, when i know that my god is jesus christ and not any one of the 6 or 8 buffoons who i have had the pleasure of helping to deflate their egos one doctor at a time.

the next bone of contention is the dietary division, known to the rest of us as the kitchen. the food is bland and it all tastes the same. they have these packets called seasoning blend but they won't give you any unless you ask for them and if you are new to the hospital there is no way to know about them so you would never know to ask. be vigilant and ask for spices to get the ball rolling to a slightly tastier meal. is it the system or the employees? i would like to believe its the system because the employees of the kitchen seem nice. i order 2 scoops of mashed potatoes with lots of gravy in a bowl and 5 packets of seasoning. i also order pureed pears, and was specific about how much i hate applesauce and please do not substitute applesauce for pureed pears. (i'm stuck on the puree diet) what do i receive? 2 scoops of mashed potatoes on a plate, no gravy, no seasoning salt or pepper, 2 pre-packaged applesauce's no pureed pears! wtf? did the lady not hear the order on the phone? i look at the slip, it clearly says 2 scoops mashed potatoes, no gravy, there's no mention of any spices and it states pureed pears. so whats the problem? maybe the person who takes the order is not the fulfillment person. and maybe the person who fulfills the order is illiterate or does not read the orders then throws whatever they want on the tray and sends some fool to deliver it to the room. bottom line, be prepared to put in your order twice, on every meal. they never get it right the first time. i hear the dj in my head say: "at palmdale regional medical center, our kitchen has you covered, when you put in your order, we will never get it right the first time, we guarantee it!" (this happens 3 times a day, its really annoying)

the er, always and i mean always enter pmrc or any hospital through the er, why? because if you are on obamacare or medi-cal you are not required by law to pay the difference between what the insurance pays on your behalf and the total retail bill! (search california balance billing, specifically ab72 and ab1611) since there is no number system, no name system because of hipaa laws, you have to constantly bug the overworked admissions person as to your place in line. 

i have suggested on more than one occasion that they install 3 or 4 tv's on the walls, everyone takes a number, then a recording plays an announcement every 15 to 30 minutes alerting the people waiting that the number is for id purposes but that all patients are taken in the order of severity. at least then it would operate more like the dmv and the people working in the er might be a tad more pleasant to deal with. the fact of the matter is, you are going to wait, so bring stuff to entertain yourself, a phone charger, a 3 way outlet thing, some usb cords etc, so you are ready to camp in the er until your name is called.

the good

the nurses and other support staff are wonderful once you get out of the er and into a room. i have stayed on every floor and lots of nurses know me by name because i am outgoing and have generally a cheerful and positive attitude. i treat them with respect and i get treated with respect in return. the nurses bust their asses every day dealing with sick people who sometimes throw feces or urine on them, treat them like personal slaves or drive them nuts nitpicking every little thing until anyone would dread helping that patient again. i have great respect for the numerous people, not just nurses, but the entire support staff at pmrc for their commitment to the patients who stay in the hospital. me being one of them! i feel a genuine sense of kindliness and good will that emanates from the dedicated nurses, anesthesiologists, xray technicians, ultrasound staff, etc.

the main reason for this post is that the er staff mishandled information that caused them to break hipaa and i now have the personal information of a previous patient of this hospital. i do not believe this was intentional, but was a very careless mistake. there were several instances where this could have been caught prior to myself noticing it at the end of our visit. 

on tuesday morning 2/18 my boyfriend was not well and asked to be taken to the er and we went to broward hospital imperial point. due to his level of pain he was distracted and asked if i could handle the signing in and provided at check in with his driver's license and completed the intake form. 

after maybe 10 minutes the nurses came in to set my boyfriend up with an iv drip, etc. we were seen by the er doctor/pa (john marini), who came in to talk to my boyfriend who was in a lot of pain so i was assisting with some of the questions. due to where the pain was located the doctor ordered for an ultrasound of his abdomen and morphine for the pain. 

question #1: why are basic questions not being asked prior to ordering expensive tests? it is the middle of flu season and patient comes in with abdominal pain after vomiting for 5 hours. no pain over mcburney's point. at no time during the entire visit did anyone ask about if he had the flu shot, would he like a flu shot, or do any kind of test swabs for the flue.  immediately they went for more expensive tests. 

the er doctor/pa came to discuss that it looked like from the ultrasound that something with his gallbladder and pancreas, and that he wanted to order a ct scan. at this time another girl, administrative, rolled in a cart with a computer and began to go over basic patient information, much of what i had literally just filled out on the intake form or could be found on his license. doctor/pa was still present, as well as another nurse. 

the girl went through the list - name, birthday, address, emergency contact, etc. none of the information that they had on file was what i had filled out and we didn't recognize anything...

question #2: is it not protocol to ask the patients for their birthday and then the patient provides it? this girl was literally reading off what was on file, and each item we had no idea where that information was coming from. they had the wrong address, wrong birthday, we had never heard of the person that was the emergency contact. at no point during this initial confirmation of information did anyone ask him for his ssn, or i'm sure this would have been caught immediately. 

they took my boyfriend for a ct and he eventually returned. the doctor/pa returned to let us know that it didn't show any issues, that his gallbladder was contracted and nothing wrong with his pancreas (not shocking, ordered an expensive test for nothing without checking off all of the other things that it could be first). he would get us set up to be discharged. he also made some kind of comment that my boyfriend had been to the er back in 2015, which my boyfriend has never been there. 

while we continued to wait and i was holding my boyfriend's hand, at that point i noticed that the birthday on his wristband was incorrect. and that was when it clicked in my head that they 100% had some other patient's information and did not have the right patient. 

i went up to the girl who had been confirming all the information before and told her "the birthday on his wristband is wrong. when we were going over information before, we didn't know the emergency contact, you had the wrong address and phone number, are you sure  you have the right person?". she looked concerned and rolled her computer back in. now, finally, one of the first questions that she asked was for him to confirm the last 4 digits of his ssn. when he did, her eyes got wide with an 'oh s***' kind of look. so i directly asked her "is what i think is happening actually happening?" and she quietly said that she thought that i was right. i asked if that changed anything that had just happened here today, and she said "it doesn't change anything for you guys but it changes a lot for me" and rolled her little cart out. i have no idea if she fixed it or if she reported it.

after all of that, somehow the prescriptions and the documents that have personal information written on them still have the wrong birthday, wrong phone number wrong address. they are someone else's, whoever was there in 2015 apparently. searching the address on google i find that it was associated with someone who has the same first and last name as my boyfriend (different middle initial) and the name of the person that they had originally told us was his listed emergency contact. i can literally google map image their home. i could call this person's phone number if i wanted to because i have it due to the hospital's mistakes.

if i could give zero stars, i would. last october, i came down with intense flank pain, sweating, and nausea. it was a kidney stone. i knew because it was not my first kidney stone and those symptoms are hard to forget. my employer told me to leave work early and get medical care.

i tried an urgent care first, but they refused care because they didn't have imaging equipment to diagnose a kidney stone. i asked google for the closest hospital, because i was in too much pain to drive but had no one else to drive me so i needed to get there as soon as possible.

i checked in to ahmc emergency room at 12:30pm but was not attended to (other than a urine test) until 3:00pm despite being in so much pain that i was writhing and rocking, and had short/ragged breaths. and yes, i had taken pain relievers... 4 excedrin migraine, which did absolutely nothing for my pain.

once i got into a bed at 3:00pm, where i sat without treatment or fluids for another hour. finally, at 4:00pm, i was given toradol which relieved my pain for about 30 minutes, and 1 liter of saline. then, at 4:30pm, the doctor came to chat with me for about 30 seconds and tell me he thinks i'm an alcoholic because i have pancreatitis (a pathology which can also happen if you're in extreme duress, which i had been for 5 hours) and that he's holding me overnight.

i'm not in the habit of disobeying doctors' orders, so i allowed this and informed my employer immediately. no one on the hospital staff would tell me approximately how long i would be hospitalized, only that i would be going upstairs.

well, upstairs was even worse. i didn't get there until 6:15pm (nearly 2 hours after any pain relief had long-since disappeared), and an hour passed before i was even 'checked in'. around 10pm i was finally given pain medication, but they didn't bother to ask me what medications i respond to, just asked if i had any 'tolerance issues' (code for, "are you a drug addict"). well no, i'm not, but i am an advocate for myself when it comes to pain management and morphine, which they gave me, only causes chest pain and severe anxiety.

i immediately expressed this after the nurse gave me the morphine, because i felt the familiar symptoms, and he said, "oh, well give it some time."

i suffered for 6 more hours without seeing another person's face, although i could hear them talking just outside my room and ignoring my moaning/crying from the pain. the next time someone checked on me, it was 4am. i begged for something different, even the toradol that i was given downstairs because it worked. the nurse said he'd have to check with the doctor on call. i didn't see him again for hours and when he did come back he said the doctor refused the toradol because it's "bad for the kidney," all the while i've been given just 2l of fluid for the past 18 hours. hey, idiots, kidney stones don't spontaneously pass. you have to flush them with fluid.

i finally did get a norco at 10:30am, which meant that about 18 hours passed while i was in 11/10 levels of pain and completely unable to sleep or focus on anything else to take my mind off of the pain... and, once again, listening to nurses talk about other patients while they were right outside my door and had to have heard my cries. furthermore, they would not allow me to take any of my regular medications, which meant 1) no anxiety medication, 2) no sleep medication, and 3) no depression medication when i was still there the next morning.

i begged to be discharged, because they were doing nothing to treat my pain or the cause of my pain. and it still took until 5:30pm (seven hours after the norco) for me to actually be discharged so that i could drink water and pass the stone, which i did in a walgreens bathroom while waiting for the azo and diuretics they had prescribed.

a couple of months later, i got a bill that stated my insurance (which was a 10% coinsurance, mind you) covered all but $900. the original bill was over $18,000. there were fees on the list that looked completely fraudulent, like a $700 charge to assess pulmonary function. unless that was how much my pulse-ox cost, there is no reason i should have a charge for pulmonary assessment. and my 2 liters of saline? $298.

so there you have it -- 30 hours of my life wasted on lack of treatment, only to receive a $900 bill.

since this incident led to me losing my job because my boss felt like i had taken a "vacation" without warning, i didn't have the energy to fight the bill. i just paid it. but you should do anything you can to avoid this hospital like it's the actual plague. walk, take the bus or a taxi, or pay a random stranger to take you to another hospital because all you'll get here is people ignoring you and then asking for ungodly amounts of money for it.
