briefly worked as a travel nurse here.  this hospital should be investigated and shut down.  the amount of fraud, medical malpractice, and genuine incompetence is stunning.  i actually wrote a letter with all of the things i saw to the local news station but they never followed up with me. 

in the 3 months i was there i watched the hospital fail 3 cms inspections and were still being given a 4th shot as the only other hospital in inglewood had already been shut down so they are serving and underserved population.  i've worked at several inner city and county hospitals and i understand the difficulties of serving that population and finances but the things that happen here are borderline if not actually criminal. 

first off it's staffed entirely by new grad nurses.  california nurse jobs are fiercely competitive so without experience or knowing someone you could end up unemployed easily.  so bright eyed new nurses come here to get their one year, see how horrible the place is run, and jump ship at day 365.  i routinely saw nurses with under one year of experience being placed in charge of their cardiovascular icu!  for staff they can't fill in they hire foreign nurses and lock them into these joke of contracts for several years that pay less than a staff position in texas. sadly they will happily take it as there isn't much of an alternative when you need your green card.

management is profoundly incompetent.  highly aggressive, low key threats, inability to accept advice or critique for quality improvement. it's the typical "filipino mafia" running things here.  for anyone not aware, the filipino mafia is a term nurses use for facilities that are primarily filipino run with a culture of "us vs you".  they are fiercely loyal to each other and will burn anyone who rocks the boat.  sadly they don't realize their boat is sinking around them. 

the physicians here are stunningly incompetent and lazy.  running ventilators on a peep of 0?! that's truly malpractice. no wonder nobody ever got better.  one physician has signs posted all around the nurses station - "do not call me for anything overnight unless it's an emergency! i will put in orders in the morning."  yeah when that emergency finally happened, 5 hours of calling later never heard back from him and sadly the patient didn't make it to the morning. 

respiratory therapy was useless, angry, and bitter.  how dare you call them for your desatting vented patient when they are in the middle of a breathing treatment in the room literally next to you?

they don't pay overtime.  they would make their staff clock out and go back to work until they finished all their work. travelers just wouldn't get paid overtime at all.  they would deny it even when you had to stay over several hours because half their day shift has called in sick or just didn't feel like showing up!

one nurse routinely would come in 2 full hours late everyday.  she claimed she drove in from far away?  yeah no, she had another full time nursing job and would finish that one and come to her other full time nursing job! but how is that possible? when would she sleep? on the job of course.  she'd get a good 5 hours in every shift and the staff around her would be stuck taking care of her patients.  but hey, she's part of the same mafia so nobody is gonna say anything to her.

call light system....was those bells that you ding ding ding like at the front of a hotel lobby. no joke you'd hear all these bells and you'd wander the hall trying to figure out who was calling.

and so much more.  none of this stuff is normal.  this is a criminal organization role playing as a hospital.  you would literally be better off dying at home than coming to this place.  i was asked to extend here but i told them i felt like a bad person working there.

where do i begin.  this has taken place during the covid-19 lock down-no family, no visitors. i had to rely on the nursing staff to keep me abreast of my 85-year-old sisters condition. you can only hope that you and your loved one are never put in this hideous, stressful situation! although, my sister was walking when admitted, a few days later she could not walk and her speech didn't sound right, kind of slurred. (could not get out of bed). i requested a phone call from the doctor, but never got one.

i discovered that she was put on the covid-19 floor even though she did not have the virus. i was told that everyone goes to that unit until their test comes back negative twice. then they are moved to another floor.

the day after she was admitted i called her and there was an ear piercing alarm going off in her room. her door was shut and the call button was not within her reach. she was in tears because this noise was nonstop for who knows how long and it was ear deafening! she said it goes off in the middle of the night when she is sleeping and wakes her.  i immediately hung up and called the nurses station. when the nurse picked up her phone i told her the situation and she literally laughed! oh yes, she said, when you have an intravenous tube in your arm that alarm goes off if you bend your elbow. i was in disbelief! how could you subject an 85 year old to this who can't get out of bed and can't reach her call button and you have her door closed?

also, her phone was put in a place where she could not reach it when i called. this happened more than once! trying to get someone at the nurses desk/station to help with this situation was a horrendous experience!!! if they answer the phone they might transfer you to your loved ones nurse who might answer their phone, but might not.

 one day i called the nurses desk for the second time because i couldn't reach my sister, and the nurse that picked up could hear me fine until i asked to speak to my sisters nurse.  she then did the "hello? hello? hello? i can't hear you" act and then hung up on me.  her name is bethany on the third floor.  she could hear me fine! 

 two days later, after putting in 8 phone calls in over a half hour, i finally got my sisters nurse, who had to check first to see if she was his patient, although i was told later that he had seen her that morning. i told him what i had been through and how frustrated i was at that point so he than told me he would walk in there with his phone so i could talk to her, but once again the phone hung up before that happened. my 9th phone call, the operator told me she would connect me to the floor supervisor who assured me he would make sure that my sisters nurse would call me right back.

he called and told me he was with my sister but that he was having a hard time waking her. she would open her eyes but than close them immediately. he said "i don't know if this is her base line."
i couldn't believe my ears. no, i said this is not her baseline! he didn't know her baseline? he had not been informed when he came on shift of the condition of his patients? she is like you or i, very alert, talking and awake during the day. there's something wrong with her! i don't know how long she was in this state. 

turns out they thought she had a stroke! they hadn't even noticed! thank goodness i insisted the nurse go in and check on her! later the neurologist called who hadn't even examined my sister, this was on may 26th, and told me the report said she had fainted. when i questioned this, in a smart ass way her reply was "were you there? because the last time i checked relatives and visitors are not allowed in the hospital because of covid-19." (i wish i could remember her name.) yes, i was there, on the phone, and she did not faint! 

they claimed it was a sudden change, that she was awake and talking that morning. so i ask why did the nurse not know that comatose was not her baseline then.? it just doesn't add up.

my sister is still there and today she was not answering her phone again. when i called the nurses station for room 428 the nurse that picked up told me that "her board did not show that anyone was in that room". what????????? she has been in that room now for 2 days.  i hung up and called the hospital operator who assured me that my sister was in room 428 and asked if i would like to be connected with her nurses cell phone. thank goodness for the operators at fawcett memorial hospital. they were the only ones that were truly helpful. if it weren't for them i would have gone out of my mind!

we still haven't gotten to the bottom of what actually happened to my sister and we probably will never know. there's more, but i've already written a book! im praying my sister will be released from there tomorrow.

needless to say, we are done with fawcett memorial hospital!

why is this company being abusive? $450 co pay for a single visit is steep ( recall that my insurance had already paid $1049 to the hospital + $798 the dr. networking company envision received from the insurance company + $450 that i co paid = $2,297  for a visit that only the nurse attended to me for 10 minutes and advised me to buy an over the counter skin cream  - to try and resolve the problem i was experiencing.

after more that a week in a hospital, thursday, late evening, i was told that my mother will be discharge on saturday. i reminded that home care agency needs to be informed, hospital bed, oxygen tank, lifting equipment etc delivered and installed. i was told not to worry! next morning  (friday), while driving to the hospital, i received a phone call. i was told that my consent is needed for special iv line for my mother, as she must be on iv medication for 4 days. i was confused, as this totally contradicted what i was told only few hours ago, so i said that i need to talk to somebody to understand what is going on and will be in a hospital in 30 min or so. when i came to the hospital..... i was told that my mother discharged today and i can take her home! i asked about the iv line etc and was told that she can take meds in a form of pills. i went to the room to see my mother. cardiologist made his rout, and told me that she is not responding to the meds and not getting better. i told him about meds on a table, about "discharging" ordeal, and he was very disturbed by it and sad that he is not discharging patient in this condition! few minutes later a man walk in the room and gave me paper to sign for portable oxygen tank to be use while transporting my mother home. he said he got order for it as my mother being discharge!

avoid this hospital at all cost!

i can't speak to the services at rwj rahway hospital, itself, nor the quality of patient care you can hope to receive.  however, i can speak to the amazing community programs the hospital runs.  if the support groups run by the hospital are indicative of its patient care, i have to say the organization is truly invested in health.  

rwj rahway, at one of its namesake gyms, rwj fitness & wellness, offers community-based support groups.   i personally attend the fibromyalgia support group & i can only describe it as a "life-saver."  before the covid-19 pandemic, we were already a close-knit group who discussed the countless lifestyle/medication/nutrition/exercise changes we'd made to improve our situation.  but, when we all went into lockdown, we had unique issues.  

led by an rn who could not care more about us if she tried, our meetings are a mix of scientific information (some unfolding & yet untested) & anecdotal experience.  

i've seen an amazing increase in my health from (regularly) attending these community meetings.  but, & more importantly during this crisis, i've had the support from people who understand our special risks & needs.  people i'm proud to now call "friends."

during this time, rwj & mindy, our group coordinator, have made zoom support group meetings.  it has been a lifesaver, when we can't be physically close, to keep this sense of emotional community makes it seem less abnormal.

- i'm not sure where to share my frustration but decided to start here.

having had a severe sore throat, cough and congestion for about a week, i went to my doctor (wearing a mask they gave me) yesterday.  i was told that i likely just had a severe sinus infection (non-contagious) but that i should probably consider being tested for covid 19.  they suggested that i go to the drive through testing at baptist east; so i did.

there was a quick drive through triage with two stops to determine that i "qualified" for testing.  then they instructed me to park my car, where i was called on my phone and told it was my turn for testing.  this all took no more than 10 minutes.  when i arrived at the first of two stops at the testing tent, i was asked for my insurance card and asked how much i wanted to put toward my $1400 deductible.  when i asked what the cost would be for the test, they told me that they did not know but that i would need to pay "something" toward my deductible for the emergency department visit.  emergency department visit!  you have to be kidding me!   those visits cost hundreds, if not thousands, of dollars and i was in a rickety tent in a parking lot trying to do my part to determine if i had exposed anyone to a terrible virus.   i got nowhere when asked why this was considered an emergency department visit instead of a minor medical or minute clinic visit.  i also told the payment staff that they should disclose the approximate cost at the very beginning of the testing process.  nonetheless, i put $50 on my credit card and proceeded to the second section of the tent to be tested for the common good.

two nurses swarmed me as i sat down in the testing section of the tent.  one took vitals while the other gave me a new set of sinus windows with five different swabs.  when i asked why so many, i was informed that they are testing for the flu, strep, covid 19 and one or two other tests.  five tests in all.  i told her that i had no idea they were going to do all those tests but she said that's what they are testing for at the current time.  and i am sure they are profiting for each and every separate test for each and every person being tested.  i went back to my car, a bit stunned from the encounter, and comforted my bleeding nostril with a tissue.

the covid-19 testing at baptist east took less that being in line at chic-fil-a and should definitely not be billed as an emergency department visit.  i feel that the hospital is taking advantage of the pandemic instead of doing its share to help those affected.  they should know better.  and they should be ashamed.

i wish you good luck with your loved ones in combating this dreadful disease.

after calling to review these charges with bon secours customer service they informed us that we would have to take this issue up with the billing department of the doctor's office.  once we spoke with the doctor's office they said that it was a bill from saint mary's hospital and would have to be handled by them.  after calling bon secours back, they gave me the name of a contact that all billing complaints go through.  they refused to give me her email or phone number.  they said all issues must be through hand written letters.  we contacted her stating our issues and after some time received a letter back.  the contact only offered services which are openly provided through customer service (pay balance right now 15% discount or set up monthly payment plan).  wrote contact back trying to get explanation of charges and cited local health care cost averages for ultrasounds.  stated that these charges were billed unethically (as if we were admitted in the hospital) and that costs of services were not within market value and were not discussed with us ahead of time.  we waited a couple months and heard nothing back.  we called their customer service and they told us our letter was received and under review.  we waited a couple more months and a collection notice came in the mail from bon secours.  we called their customer service back and let them know about this issue and that it had been under review.  they stated the bill was unpaid and therefore sent to collections.  we were never able to speak with anyone with autonomy, were billed extremely unethically and nobody from their organization would directly communicate with us about their bill.  my wife and i have high credit scores and always pay our bills in accordance with our responsibilities.  this company refused to openly communicate with us or explain their absurd billing practices.  buyers beware!!! we had our baby at alta bates and we were so impressed by the level of care we received. i have to admit, i was a bit apprehensive after taking a hospital tour a few weeks before my delivery. the maternity floor could use a major facelift and the rooms we visited were small and dark.

i went into labor several days before the shelter-in-place order was announced but the hospital was already taking precautions to ensure that everyone was screened at the entrance. 

every staff member we met throughout our experience was professional, kind, and caring. the triage nurse was warm and made me feel calm in what could be a nervous start for a first time mom. our labor and delivery nurse was dedicated to us during the entire labor and rarely left the room. there were a couple of instances where the baby's heart rate dropped and our nurse had to call backup. within seconds, four other nurses showed up and they quickly rectified the situation. the nurses clearly have strong working relationships with one another and demonstrated the type of teamwork we all strive to achieve (but rarely do).

once the baby was delivered, i was wheeled to the recovery portion of the floor. there, each new shift of caretakers - nurse, nurse assistant, charge nurse, and lactation consultant came to check on us and made sure we had everything we needed from diapers for the baby (and me) to water and food for my fiance. we were extremely well taken care of.

what made my experience even better was that the rooms i was assigned to were a huge upgrade over the ones we had seen during the tour. our labor & delivery room had a jacuzzi tub and was one of the largest on the floor. the recovery room, where we spent almost three days, was also spacious enough for baby, fiance, guests, and me. we visited friends at kaiser when they had their baby and while that hospital is more modern, their room was much smaller than what we had here.

overall, no complaints at all and i'm really satisfied with my experience.

i've given birth to both my girls here in 2007 and 2012 and will be giving birth here for the third and last time due in march. the nurses have always been helpful and kind however, after giving birth, i feel like they need to give us moms a break. this review is based on my 2012 experience. they come in just about every single hour for every little thing when you're trying to rest after being in labor and pushing for however many hours. i chose to breastfeed my kids but at one point with my second daughter, i asked for some formula so that my husband could help just so i could sleep a bit because baby didn't want to get off my boobs and cried the whole time if she wasn't on it and the nurse refused and kept telling me i had to keep her on the boob even after seeing how exhausted i was and crying. i find it so damaging mentally and emotionally to basically tell an overly exhausted mom that she pretty much cannot sleep because if baby wants to be on the boob 24/7 (regardless if you already nursed 15-20 mins every 3 hours) then she needs to just be on the boob 24/7, no formula. no pacifier. formula or breastfeeding should be a mother's choice, not something forced upon by the hospital! and if a mom who just went through labor asks for formula just to get 2-3 hours of sleep, then they should be able to grant that. my last hospital stay was overly draining and i plan on packing formula and bottles and a pacifier with this birth because i can't imagine having to endure 2 1/2 days of no sleep again and being told i can't do something


update: i would love to thank all the nurses who helped cared for myself and my son these past few days. i had an amazing experience with em all. can't remember everyone's name i encountered but to list who i can remember - giselle, stacey, brooke, erika, ana (so thankful for your extra kindness on my last day), anna, angie, maria, sally and a handful of others. 

to the awesome rn's i got the pleasure to have encountered in nicu - idonna, lina, kayla and dr. tan. and the two secretaries/receptionist in front; you guys are truly a god send. there aren't enough words and praises in this world to describe how amazingly badass you women are! especially idonna and kayla who i felt really wanted my son to get better quickly and went above and beyond while also having their hands full with other babies. thank you, thank you, thank youu from the bottom of my heart!!!

#1 son had swelling on his face and feeling lethargic and urgent care saw something suspicious on his chest x-ray so they sent us here to the ermmediately. 

this is my first experience with this hospital, it is closest to our new retirement town and it takes approximately 20-25 minutes by car to get here unless of course the seasonal traffic is heavy. that's a big change for me since,  in all the 12 states that i have lived in, i have always been pretty close to an er. but it is what it is. 

the covid protocols are very strictly enforced here, there's a person asking questions and taking temperatures outside and they give you a mask if you don't have one. they only allow adult patients to enter however i am my son's medical proxy so i accompanied him for the whole process. 

the wait didn't look bad at all however the urgent care called ahead and we were taken right away. i worked in er's for several years both in the navy and in a civilian trauma center so my critique will be from an insiders prospective.

the receptionists demeanor, efficient and professionalism was very good. we made it through the paperwork and were taken back very quickly. once inside there was a triage nurse who whisked us into an exam bay, two other nurses quickly hooked matt up to a monitor and got his vitals while putting in an iv line. they drew blood from the iv, which proved to later be a problem, and the portable x-ray was done within minutes. 

a phlebotomist arrived in approximately ten minutes to draw five new tubes of blood commenting that the nurses needed to get up to speed on their, apparently new, iv setups as the original draws had hemolized. that's an unfortunate error because blood sticks are sometimes difficult and of course more unnecessary blood draws are not a good practice for time and for the patient. 

moving on, dr. ronnie sims came in within a half hour of our arrival and assured us that the chest x-ray was just fine and after asking some good questions he just wanted to draw another set of enzymes to make sure that there were no cardiac issue. 

the blood draw was taken quickly however the turnaround was an hour, which could have been done in fifteen minutes, but once they got the results we were expeditiously discharged out and we're on our way. 

there's no way for me to know if our experience was typical for this er, since we have nothing to compare it to, but overall they staff did a very nice job. 

bottom line: #1 son is well and this hospital er does a very nice job!

recent covid 19 update! do not deliver your baby at st francis medical center!!

ok so where do we start. my wife and i were waiting in anticipation for the birth of our baby girl. our obgyn at all safe medical group,  referred us to st francis & said they were highly recommended. so that was the plan.

2 months prior to giving birth in march we kept trying to call to pre register & no one would pick up the phone, despite leaving numerous voice mail messages & calling many times.

now we are 2 days out from giving birth. cut to 2 days past our due date (april 29th) when she started getting contractions & again had continually tried to call with no luck getting a hold of someone. finally after 4 phone calls throughout the day, someone finally picked up the phone. he said that there is no one available to check guests in and to just come in when her contractions are 5 minutes apart. after pushing back and explaining that we were upset with the lack of follow up, he revealed that the girl in charge of registering patients had just been furloughed by the hospital due to covid19 and to just come in and someone would take care of her. 

on the night of sunday may 1st, 2020 at 10.30pm the contractions hit my wife hard and fast and she was in excruciating pain. 

once we arrived, a nurse at the front checked us for covid related systems. neither of us had any symptoms & i explained that i just had surgery and was tested for covid 19 & was negative. the nurse then said unemotionally that unfortunately they are not allowing a support person to come into the delivery ward until the patient is 10cm dilated, and at the point would then be submitted into the room for pregnancy but would have to leave once the baby is born & would not be able to stay during recovery. as this was our first child, and we were both already scared and nervous, my wife instantly bursted into tears, and kept saying she can't do this without me. she was begging me not to leave while nurse was edging her to come with her. 

at first, i tried to calmly explain & the nurse that i was covid free & she kept unemotionally and unapologetically repeating company policy. i said it didn't make sense, and said if i am covid free or was re-tested (which i was prepared to do) then why would they not let me in.

then this extremely obnoxious security guard starting screaming at us saying that it was part of cdc guidelines & they were just doing their job. at this point (understandably) i was distraught with the lack of empathy and kindness. they both kept telling my wife to come hack & we both looked at each other and said f*ck this, we are not staying here. it was disgraceful, especially as the security guard continued to yell at us and my wife's mother who said this was unfair and not right.

we pulled ourselves together & then called 2 other hospitals in la (adventist health white memorial & la county usc) mid her heavy & painful contractions while in tears crying. both hospitals said that she (the patient) would have to be tested and that if she was negative, they would allow me (one support person) to not only stay with her prior to giving birth but also in recovery, but said the covid test may take a few hours). i just would not be able to leave the hospital.

we decided on white memorial because the night before i had ankle surgery there and we were both blown away by all of the staff's kindness, empathy and the way they communicated to us. looking back, this was the best decision we could face ever made. i had to wait in the car for 3 hours for my wife to get a covid test, but after it came back clear i was finally allowed in. my wife was in labor for 27 hours before she gave birth and then we stayed for another 24hours in recovery. the staff went above and beyond and were the kindest nicest people we have both ever met. everyone was so accommodating and went above and beyond to make sure our stay was comfortable. i couldn't imagine her being alone for all that time. the actually birth only took 20 mins so what good what have that been to her?

what this leads me to believe was that st francis's stance on support guests during covid 19, had nothing to do with the cdc guidelines, rather their own personal hospital guidelines. 

st francis medical center, how dare you, treat my wife with such a lack of compassion & empathy, especially during such a scary time. we are fair!& rational people & understand there are some accommodations that need to be made, but covid 19 aside, believe that that is no excuse for being unprofessional, rude & unkind.

for anyone considering giving birth here, i would never recommend this hospital to anyone, especially if you want to bring a support guest, partner or husband with you, which i'd imagine is every women on the planet.

just created an anonymous profile on here to keep my dad's info somewhat private and write a review that is long overdue, but what better time than national nurse's day to write my review right?! 

i just want to first start by thanking all those involved in the care of my father, in early january, before all this covid pandemonium started. he unfortunately had a stroke and suffered much of the loss of motor function to the right side of his body. as you can imagine, this took quite a toll on my dad and our family. 

as we went in to see my dad everyday to be there for support, there was one nurse in particular that i wanted to send a very special shout out to. his name his aaron and he works on the recovery unit next to the mri building. 

although we encountered a number of amazing staff members, aaron sticks out to myself and my family for our own reasons. i know we were not always easy to deal with during that frustrating time, and aaron was always composed, empathetic, never left us in the dark, and always made us feel like our time was extremely valuable to him. 

but ultimately, the reason i chose to recognize him on national nurse's day, is for what he did after my dad was discharged from northbay to a rehab center in napa. on that day, he told my dad he'd try to visit him and check on his progress if that was okay. lo and behold, two days later, on a saturday, there was aaron to the surprise of us all. he took time from his day off to visit my dad and offer words of encouragement. aaron ended up spending the entire day with my dad and our family until visiting hours were over. 

oh gosh! i'm crying now, so let me wrap this up. aaron, if you get to read this, i just want to say how incredibly grateful we are to you for being the nurse that you are, but more so, for just being the kind-hearted human being that you are, which isn't always easy to find these days. your mom raised an amazing young man, and never change k. happy national nurse's day. 

with love, from our family to yours, 
amy

i want to write a review on the inpatient dining "expressly for you." there is a menu that you can order what you want. there are specific times that you must be followed in ensure your meal order is placed in time. i have ordered many things from the menu, overall, i think they try to be to fancy and offer too many complex meal options. when i am sick, i prefer to eat very simple things without a ton of spice or flavor. this may just be me, but here are some of my thoughts on things i have ordered. 

scrambled eggs: the first time i ordered scrambled eggs they arrived with onions and peppers. this was not expected. the next time i ordered, i specified that i wanted scrambled eggs plain without onions or peppers. this time it arrived with a garnish orange slice that spread orange juice on my eggs and rendering them inedible. if you just want eggs, order without garnish! 

oatmeal: this is a solid basic. it is pretty bland by itself, but would highly recommend adding banana slices and a packet of cream cheese. 

pimento cheese plate: this is a generous scoop of pimento cheese and served with fresh veggies and pita. i wasn't feeling up to eating much, but what i did eat was great! 

cheeseburger and fries: one night i didn't get a dinner order placed, so they brought me a late tray option. it was a freshly made burger and fries. i may have just been super hungry, but this was amazing!! 

chicken salad sandwich: this was okay. the chicken salad had too much mayo for my taste, but not bad. 

chicken tenders: there was a lot of breading, but easy to peel off.

baked potato: good simple option and can order shredded cheese and sour cream on the side.

clear liquid diet: i'm not sure much can be done to make this better, but this is rough! the tray comes with broth (i sampled vegetable, chicken, and beef), jello, juice, or flavored water. the broth was always luke warm and never appealing, but this is likely a result of how i was feeling. pro tip:  the floors stock popsicles, so that is a great alternative/supplement to the tray. 

if you miss ordering off the menu or get to your room late the floors stock some boxed meals. one night my diet was advanced from clears to regular diet late and i wanted solid food. they brought me a turkey sandwich boxed lunch. i ate the turkey (not then bread) a standard basic turkey sandwich which is a good option when the cafeteria is closed. 

things i wish were on the menu: greek yogurt. they have sugary yogurt, but i really wish there was greek yogurt, low fat string cheese sticks, plain tuna without being in tuna salad, or other high protein simple options. 

the people that take your order on the phone are really helpful and willing to get you want you want!

this review is for the labor and delivery unit. i work in healthcare, so i have a better understanding of how healthcare systems work compared to most people, and as prepared as i was to understand the finances and logistics of my pregnancy and childbirth, even i was unprepared for the problems i would have during childbirth.

first i had an issue with their billing. i called the billing department to verify that the hospital was considered in-network under my health plan, so i thought a normal vaginal delivery would be fully covered. however i was surprised to receive bills following my delivery from the anesthesia provider, who was out of network, the pediatricians who did the newborn physicals and hearing exams were out of network. overall, giving me a headache by having to sort out bills during the time i should have been bonding with my baby, rather than spending hours on the phone. as someone who is very diligent about making sure i understood everything forward and backwards regarding the cost of my delivery, i still was misinformed. lesson is: ask your insurance health plan specifically if the anesthesia providers, pediatricians, and any other providers you might see are in-network. personally, if i could do it again i would have opted to deliver at kaiser or ucla, where you know that you won't have any providers who are out-of-network. the experience of dealing with insurance providers and these other private providers have been painful to say the least. 

secondly, their "baby friendly" designation is misleading. i was very open to the myriad of possible events that can happen during childbirth, and that a lot of things are unpredictable, especially as medical events can alter the course of action. however, i felt  their nursing staff have so many traveling nurses in their unit, some who are unaware of the policies or full extent of services available in the unit, that i felt that most of them did not fully understand the services available during childbirth. for example, i asked to use the tub for pain relief, which i knew was available because it was shown to us during a tour, however there was a nurse who had no idea that there was even a tub available. i also found that the obstetrician who delivered my daughter, dr. mia sanders madati, was slow to come to my bedside once the baby started crowning. the nurse who was helping me to push literally had to tell me to hold the baby, while we waited 10 minutes for her to arrive to my bedside. as any woman who has every had to deliver a baby vaginally, every minute feels like eternity. then when the baby came, instead of putting the baby immediately on me, she took her sweet little time cleaning off the baby's face and body, when all i wanted was the baby to be on me. lesson is: you are your best advocate and also get your partner to advocate for you. understand that things may be out of your control, but don't blindly just assume what they tell you is always right. you never know what your experience will be like until you actually deliver. 

overall, having your baby is a truly special, once in a lifetime experience for some people like me, where i waited so long to have a baby. i am grateful to have had a healthy baby girl. however, if i had the chance to do it all over again, i would have chosen a different hospital to deliver.

who are the most marginalized people in our society? the elderly and the obese; and so my story begins....
after a gastric sleeve surgery to help treat my obesity, i was sent to recover in a room where my roommate was a 92 year old sweetheart who had suffered a small stroke, but was otherwise a force to be reckoned with!
directly after my surgery, i was in exquisite, terrible pain and was unable complete the first stage of the post op diet so it was determined that i would stay the night instead of going home the same day.
after my husband went home i tried to rest, but my pain was increasing and i was feeling more and more unwell. i tried to let my nurses know what was going on, but i was told that all of this was normal and that i should try to rest. in the evening at some point, i did fall asleep and the next time i awoke, i was surrounded by panicked staff and nurses who were picking me up off the floor. 
i have no idea how i got there or how long i was there. 
i found out later that it was my lovely roommate who noticed me and although she shouted and repeatedly pressed the call button, nobody came for what she described as "a long while". see where marginalized comes into play again?
my blood pressure was critically low and i don't remember too much of that night from hell except a few things;
i was sent for a barium swallow where it was found that i had internal bleeding and a large clot in my abdomen (extremely painful and not at all normal). the testing was also a very painful experience since no pain relief had been administered (tylenol only) since earlier in the evening. there was also some concern that my collarbone had broken during the fall from bed, so i also had xrays done with no pain medication after which, i sat in a wheelchair in an empty room while waiting for transportation back to my room for hours.
after being taken back to my room, my surgeon came to tell me that i should call my husband and tell him what happened?! that i should tell him?crazy right?
he also told me that i needed a blood transfusion. in the morning my sister came to visit and while there the nurses came to administer the transfusion. they told me that i needed to let them know if i suddenly felt unwell so they could intervene if i was having a reaction to the blood.
they left, and presently, i started to feel feverish so i rang the call button and the man who answered asked what i wanted. i told him that i was feeling like i might have a fever and he said, and i quote, "what do you want me to do about it" to which i replied "take my temperature?" his reply? "i guess i'll pretend to be a doctor now".
god help me , the rest of my stay didn't get any better, i felt unsafe and totally uncared for. i couldn't wait to get home, so i pretended to be improving so they would release me
my recovery took a long time and my interactions didn't get any better afterwards with my surgeon, he still thinks that i didn't loose consciousness?
i was totally traumatized then and it's still really hard to speak or write about it now almost a year later.
i would never recommend cmc to anyone i care about.

i have had both private and kaiser insurance, so i feel qualified to comment and compare the two systems.  been to private physicians in the bay area (including stanford and ucsf), have had lab and radiology services, and hospitalizations up and down the peninsula over the past 30 years.  i realize people have individual experiences that may not be like mine.

kaiser ssf is designed to handle large volumes of people more efficiently, so it is in some ways less personal medicine.  one can sometimes feel like cattle. however, i don't need a lot of hand holding, and i love kaiser ssf for its relative efficiency.  i've been going to kaiser now as my primary insurance for over 15 years, because i find my coordinated care to be far better than through private insurance.  i like the fact that i can see another doctor in the kaiser system in a timely fashion if my doctor is unavailable.  i like having my meds mailed to me. flu shots are super easy.  your preventive care schedules (immunizations, colonoscopy, mammograms etc) are tracked and you are informed in writing.  

at kaiser ssf, i have never had to wait more than 5-15 minutes for an x-ray or mri or ct or a blood draw.  er was reasonably quick the one time i was there -- i was able to check in and be seen and get a ct, then out the door in about 90 minutes.  the er doctor was kind but also very businesslike and to the point, which was appreciated. the er staff also scheduled an appointment for a specialist for the next morning, so that i wouldn't have to do it myself.  i really appreciated their thoughtfulness. in private practice facilities, i've had to wait over 2 hours for a pre-scheduled simple chest x-ray; over 30 minutes for a lab; and weeks for a doctor's appointment. 

quality of doctors --- i have had some really great doctors over the years at kaiser and outside of kaiser.  (exception: i liked my obgyn and dermatology doctors outside of kaiser better.) my internist, oncologist, and surgeon at kaiser are as knowledgeable and skillful as the ones i had outside of kaiser, but unlike the others, my kaiser doctors talk to each other so the care is coordinated each step of the way.  

my personal feeling is that private practice care is fractured -- the doctors can't talk to each other, and reimbursements with in-network/out-of-network facilities and providers are a real pain. it's sad, and all created because some mbas out there thought they had a better business model.  they broke it, and we will never have american medicine the way it used to be.

they are trying to charge me for a level 4 (levels start at 1 and go up to 5- 5 is the most serious and most expensive) service charge. that alone is over $3,000- the charges add up to almost $6,000 not including my insurance coverage. now, i know i walked into an emergency room, and that it would cost more than my less-than-a-hundred-dollars copay, but really?? everything that was done that day could have been done by my doctor and the lab for under $100. i decided i wouldn't dispute the charges for the lab work, doctor's fee, and ultrasounds- but the level 4 charge needed to be reduced. the price is absolutely unjust and unreasonable for the standard service i received.

i called sutter, who directed me to my insurance company, called them and realized the issue was not my insurance...   i called sutter again, was given a number for something i didn't need- i can't tell you how many times i have called or how many people i have talked to, but i would say i talked to at least 5 of the regular billing department agents, and then i asked to escalate it, that was another person, and then i was told to take it up with the er doctor directly, called the er department who gave me to the department manager who needed to talk to the next person...  this has been going on since march. i have played endless phone tag, left messages, and i've gotten the run-around. it is now almost the end of may and i still haven't talked to anyone who can do anything about anything, and i'm damn tired of people trying to explain things to me, when they can't give me answers to questions i have been asking. it is almost time for my bill to get shoveled over to collections because they refuse to help me.

doc_text:
renown medical center delivers a ridiculous amount of babies every day (4,063 in the year 2016), especially with being one of the main hospitals in reno (next to st. mary's) and from experience, i can easily see that they know what they're doing.

i'm the mother of three children and two of them were born at renown medical center.  my experiences were nothing short of amazing.  the ease of check in, skill level of the doctors, nurses and staff, resources available, and level of comfort all contributed to my amazing experiences and i would easily come back to renown if i ever planned on having another child.

my second child, arrived in half the time as my first child. instead of 12 hrs., he arrived in 6 hrs. i was at home laboring it out when my water broke and i knew he would come out shortly.  my dear sister zoomed us to the emergency section of the hospital knowing i wouldn't have time to check in and upon arrival, someone with a chair wheeled me into the delivery room.  the nurses heard me coming down the hall and my sister said they all quickly flocked together in a group, waiting to receive me.

they transferred me to the bed and immediately called the doctor.  the doctor arrived promptly and was very skillful with how he delivered my baby.  he did a technique that prevented tares and i couldn't have been happier since my first birthing experience left me in pain with a third degree tare.  asking your doctor ahead of time about ways to prevent tares could be beneficial so as to minimize healing time post delivery.

after my baby came out, the nurses quickly wiped him with towels and placed him on my chest.  bonding occurs right away and it is said that skin to skin contact also helps calm babies while keeping them warm and helps trigger your milk supply for breastfeeding.  they also applied antibiotic eye drops to prevent eye infections.

while holding my baby, the doctor came in and made sure the placenta came out.  one firm press to my stomach did the trick and the placenta slipped right out.

shortly after, the nurses took him to a table right next to my bed. there, they suctioned out extra fluids to help him breath better, took some measurements, and made sure everything was normal.

after being asked some questions, i was transferred to my recovery room.

in recovery, the nurse assisted me with my first bathroom break and gave me some instruction on how to care for myself.  the bathroom was fully stocked with everything i needed-underwear, pads, wash bottles, gowns and towels.   after, she offered me an ice pack for my bottom and i was so thankful since it was so soothing.

with my second baby, my husband went along with the nurses for his first bath. with the third baby, i was able to watch my baby's first bath.

they monitored me and my baby closely to make sure our vitals were on point and to make sure i was feeling ok and that i wasn't bleeding excessively.

a lactation consultant visited me to assist me with breastfeeding and any questions i had.  renown does have alternatives and resources to breastfeeding of you're unable to.

my doctor visited me the following day to see my progress and gave the o.k. to go home.  they monitor you for a minimum of 24 hrs. to make sure everything is fine but mothers usually stay 24-48 hrs. after birth.

it took a total of 10 minutes from the time i arrived to the time my baby came out.  with such little time, renown was able to deliver in all areas.  i was so impressed with how prepared they were.  there's nothing more comforting than knowing you have people you can depend on to get you through your birthing experience.

i gave birth to my three children without epidural and i wouldn't have done it any other way.  of course i was scared of the unknowns of pain that i would experience but i knew it was pain that i could handle and pain that would be worthwhile.

there are many options available for pain management at renown and different methods of giving birth.

with my second delivery at renown, i made sure to allow extra time to check in.  i went in through the front of entrance of the hospital and was checked into a screening room where they determined that i was far along to be admitted.  this time around, they called my doctor (information on hand from pre-registration) who made it just in time to deliver my third baby.  i gave birth yet again and couldn't have been happier with the service given.

renown's doctors, nurses and staff exceeded my expectations.  the beautiful hospital allowed for my husband to sleep overnight with me and the snack room (accessible to only mothers), was a pleasant surprise.

https://www.skillexpertiseandtechnology.com/obreg/

pregnancy guide made by renown:
https://www.renown.org/wp-content/uploads/pregnancyguide.pdf

*don't forget to bring baby's car seat and to install the base prior to giving birth

i continued with encompass home health when i got home -- and til the pandemic, i was crazy about both my physical therapist and my occupational therapist, both from encompass. then, when the world shut down and we were told to stay home, i asked for teletherapy. and, that's where the problems began.  encompass insisted that medicare required an in-person visit to accompany teletherapy. what?  you want me to be exposed to your therapists who are in nursing homes and with possible "compromised" patients every day? what?  i am 74 years old -- i cannot do that and you shouldn't be asking me to do that  -- an, btw,  medicare repeatedly told me that what encompass home health was claiming was 1) untrue, and, 2) impeding my recovery process. by the time i fired encompass home health, i'd gone more than 6 weeks with no therapy -- and my progress had basically stopped.  i have someone new now -- and he's great -- and is pushing me so i can hopefully make up some lost time. 
 
but if you want ongoing, consistent therapy, beware of encompass home health -- i cannot tell you how many excuses they came up with as to why they couldn't provide what everyone in the whole world was advising:  virtual care whenever possible and minimal exposure to outsiders. getting their reimbursement became much more important than ensuring my continued recovery.  i haven't even hugged my daughter for almost two months -- i was not about to allow "in-person" visits from encompass.
 
also, i found out later that my pt was in fact exposed and quite ill about two weeks after i stopped her from coming to my house.  not that encompass would have ever told me that -- and i wonder how many patients have unnecessarily been exposed to a potentially lethal virus because encompass misunderstood the medicare rules. just sayin'.....

it's very rare that i write a rating, but this was too good not to share. in january 2020, my husband and i had a phenomenal experience with the labor & delivery, maternity unit, and nicu at wellspan ephrata community hospital!!! as a nurse, pilot, and with my first delivery, i was just so blown away by how amazing the staff treated us, how beautiful and clean the facility was, and all of the effort by the staff to make us feel comfortable.

i was transferred to the ephrata for stalled labor after being awake approximately 30 hours. the staff gave me medication to assist me to get some sleep, while progressing my labor. during this time, they brought a reclining chair and cot into the delivery room for my husband and best friend, provided regular updates to my parents along with taking them to a monitor to explain what was going on, and delivered pillows and blankets to the waiting room. my husband and best friend were guided by the staff in how to best support me and be involved in the delivery. the midwives, nurses, and other staff worked to preserve my goal for a regular delivery with minimal site trauma.

when we transferred to my maternity room in the middle of the night, the staff already had a reclining chair and cot set up for my husband and best friend. thankfully i asked our nurse to take the baby since we were exhausted and not safe to care for a newborn. a few hours later our baby had a seizure. the nurse recognized it right away and immediately took him around the corner to the nicu. during my maternity admission and the baby's week long admission in the nicu, we continued to be amazed by the wonderful experience with the pediatricians, nurses, lactation consultants, and staff. the nurse to patient ratio and dedication of the staff facilitated individualized personal care. they all took the time to personally interact with us and provided a wealth of knowledge to set us up for success. in my experience as a nurse, we are stretched severely thin with balancing multiple priorities and often there just isn't enough time to get to know our patients. 

what we experienced at ephrata hospital was truly amazing and life changing. the staff were such a blessing and we are forever appreciative. we will definitely be back for the delivery of our second child! thank you, thank you!!!

i'm a 79 year old cad elder patient with many fine experiences with staff at gulf coast and health park over the years. last october i missed my veteran nurses. they were  replaced by much younger staff. in er, they were training youngsters like mad. some knew their stuff. many did not. sad so many veterans have left or retired. please explain why this has happened? . 

two weeks ago had worst er experience ever. it was at gulf coast. arrived 9 pm with painful urination. 
they scoped my bladder and took blood twice in three tries. i still have the bruise from one failure. surprised they took no urine samples.  my wife and i were also shocked at sad conditions of rest rooms. at 3 am, a very young doctor finally showed. i asked her to look at my urine, please. she did and came back at 3:45 am with a uti diagnosis from urine sample. blood told them nothing.  i arrived home exhausted and disoriented. fell asleep in my bathtub. when i woke up, one hearing aid was missing. my wife found my wet, ruined cell phone in the kitchen.  i must have knocked it in the tub while asleep.
wade m. nye

i went to sierra tuscon treatment center last year. it saved my life. was it perfect, i don't think any place can be perfect for all people. in the beginning i was very rude to most staff, i had meltdowns many times, but i felt safe. i got the right medication i need at this time in my life. everyone was very pleasant and nice, i might not have seen it at the time. i was unhappy about a lot of things but i can see now how much i needed to go through my emotions and self pity to start to heal. i learned to self advocate. i can't wish for a better place to be safe during my beginning of my healing.
with a step down program in california and a strong support at home i am having a normal functioning life.
i could wish for a better exit day than i had, but at the same time, it made me stronger, i learned i can handle things that comes up.
if i ever need a treatment center again, i would definitely choose sierra tuscon.

only day 2 but you should be aware that when you get there, you are put into a building with lots of people with different issues. you are strip searched and everything is taken away from you except your clothes.
the rooms have darkened windows so you can't see outside, the doors are locked. you have to sit around and wait for them to be ready to give you all the tests. if you have anxiety or panic attacks it is very very difficult. just be aware of this if you go. we didn't see this kind of situation on the website. maybe we missed it but we are pretty thorough. this was not expected. i hope my son sticks it out and doesn't leave but i would not blame him if he did. he is there for ptsd and this is exacerbating his anxiety and panic attacks so far. 
will write more if he makes it to treatment.
